event_name: Tantura
location: Palestinian village near Haifa
actor_as_reported: Alexandroni Brigade / emerging Israeli forces (agency attribution provisional)
event_categories: occupation; alleged executions of captives; detention; depopulation
affected_people_or_estimate: Palestinian villagers; count of killings unresolved
evidence_summary: Later survivor testimony and Israeli veteran testimony are reported; forensic spatial analysis identifies possible mass-grave sites; no exhumation or court finding in sources reviewed
evidence_status: Contested allegation with corroborating testimony and spatial evidence; denial and disagreement preserved
legal_status: No judicial finding; legal classification unadjudicated
scope_decision: Include as a sourced allegation; do not enter an exact death toll
limitations: Guardian reports estimates of 40–200, which are not a verified count. Forensic Architecture maps possible grave sites; the site was not excavated. Current scholarship differentiates village occupation/evacuation and alleged post-surrender killings. State-formation command chain on 22–23 May requires source-specific care.

event_name: Lydda (Lod) and Ramle
location: central Palestine
actor_as_reported: Israeli Army and Palmach troops (as identified by contemporary press and later research)
event_categories: military capture; mass detention of men; expulsion of civilians
affected_people_or_estimate: Thousands of men reported captive; contemporary correspondent counted 3,000–4,000 at Lydda and about 1,500 at Ramle; later scholarship estimates 60,000–70,000 expelled
evidence_summary: Contemporary U.S. newspaper report filed from Lydda; UN Mediator's 1948 report says occupation of the towns and villages augmented refugee numbers; later scholarship reconstructs forced expulsion
evidence_status: Capture and mass detention contemporaneously reported; coercive expulsion documented by later historical research; individual death/displacement counts vary
legal_status: No judicial finding in reviewed sources; investigate forcible transfer and treatment of captives under law applicable in 1948
scope_decision: Include capture, detention, and expulsion as separate linked claims; do not treat the contemporary dispatch alone as proof of the full expulsion total
limitations: Contemporary dispatch records prisoners and the town's surrender, but does not itself document the full expulsion. Later record identifies Operation Dani and the expulsion; overall refugee totals for 1948 are not attributed wholesale to Israel here.

event_name: Ein Ghazal, Jaba, Ijzim
location: south of Haifa
actor_as_reported: Israeli military forces
event_categories: air and land attacks; forced evacuation; destruction of villages; alleged killings/captures
affected_people_or_estimate: UN observers located more than 4,000 villagers; fewer than 130 were reported killed or missing; separate UN yearbook summary says more than 8,000 located
evidence_summary: UN Mediator cable and UN Yearbook summary based on UN observer investigation
evidence_status: UN investigation confirms attacks by air and land, forced evacuation, destruction of Ein Ghazal and Jaba, and failure to pursue villagers' offer to negotiate; mass-death claims were found exaggerated
legal_status: Mediator stated actions were unjustified and systematic destruction excessive, violating the spirit and letter of the truce; not a criminal judgment
scope_decision: Include UN-confirmed action and UN legal characterization; retain numerical discrepancy between source versions
limitations: Counts differ between the Mediator's cable (>4,000 located) and Yearbook summary (>8,000). Do not collapse or average. UN report says Ijzim's houses were damaged, while Ein Ghazal and Jaba were destroyed.

event_name: Israeli detention and POW/labor camps
location: multiple locations inside Israel
actor_as_reported: Israeli forces and camp authorities
event_categories: capture; civilian internment; interrogation; forced labor; reported torture, beatings, shootings and deprivation
affected_people_or_estimate: Authors estimate around 5,000 Palestinian civilian internees in four official camps; separate ICRC POW tallies include military prisoners and are not a pure Palestinian-civilian count
evidence_summary: ICRC reports and 1948 field visits, later analyzed in Journal of Palestine Studies; ICRC historical summary confirms visits to Arab POWs in Israel
evidence_status: Multiple former detainee testimonies; ICRC records cited by authors include abuse injuries, beatings and poor conditions; article reports forced labor and civilians held alongside military POWs
legal_status: Potential unlawful civilian internment, forced labor and abuse require legal analysis; no court finding in sources reviewed
scope_decision: Include detainee-treatment allegations and source-linked population estimate; do not present all POW tallies as civilian detainee totals
limitations: The JPS article draws on ICRC archives, survivor interviews and secondary research. Some torture details are survivor testimony; distinguish from direct ICRC observations. 1949 Geneva Convention postdates these events.

event_name: Central Galilee villages (including al-Bi'na and neighboring communities)
location: Galilee
actor_as_reported: Israeli forces
event_categories: Operation Hiram; mass displacement; roundup and detention of men and boys
affected_people_or_estimate: An estimated three-quarters of roughly 60,000 Palestinian Arab inhabitants displaced; hundreds of men and boys detained; about 200 men from al-Bi'na reported captured
evidence_summary: Later Journal of Palestine Studies article cites survivor testimony and a 16 November 1948 UN observer report
evidence_status: Article reports displacement during the operation and detention of noncombatant village men; evidence includes named oral testimony and UN observer report
legal_status: No judicial finding in reviewed sources; investigate civilian protection, expulsion, and detention allegations
scope_decision: Include as a documented research case with estimates attributed to the cited author and underlying records
limitations: The 60,000 figure is the estimated Arab population of the area; three-quarters is an estimate, not a household-level displacement count.

event_name: Beersheba
location: Negev
actor_as_reported: Israeli forces
event_categories: capture; expulsion to Gaza; detention and forced labor of captive men
affected_people_or_estimate: JPS article cites Ben-Gurion's diary noting around 100 men held captive, put to work, then sent to a prison camp; most of the town population was expelled to Gaza
evidence_summary: Later historical study citing Ben-Gurion's wartime diary and Palestinian detainee sources
evidence_status: Capture and displacement reported by historical sources; detention of about 100 men is tied to Ben-Gurion diary entry
legal_status: No judicial finding in reviewed sources; assess expulsion and treatment separately
scope_decision: Include as a source-linked episode; mark population count and transfer chronology for verification
limitations: Not a direct contemporary news dispatch; cross-check diary entry and refugee records before using a precise total.

event_name: al-Dawayima
location: Hebron district
actor_as_reported: Israeli forces (occupation acknowledged; alleged killings denied by Israel)
event_categories: contested massacre allegation; civilian killings
affected_people_or_estimate: No independently verified victim count in sources reviewed
evidence_summary: Arab Refugee Congress allegation recorded by UN Conciliation Commission; Israeli government's 8 November letter denies atrocity and says civilians had left before occupation
evidence_status: Contested allegation; available records include the allegation and formal denial, not a completed independent fact-finding determination
legal_status: No judicial finding in sources reviewed
scope_decision: Keep in allegation queue; do not count fatalities as confirmed until independent corroboration is found
limitations: The UN working paper preserves an Arab Refugee Congress account, while Israel's letter contests the claim and location naming. Seek UN observer notes, British records, and independent contemporaneous reporting.

event_name: Israeli air raids on Gaza
location: Gaza city
actor_as_reported: Israeli Air Force (Associated Press attribution)
event_categories: air bombing; reported civilian flight
affected_people_or_estimate: Palestinian Arab civilian population reported fleeing; no count or casualties stated
evidence_summary: Associated Press dispatch dated 19 October says Israeli bombing had entered its fourth day and civilians were reported fleeing; UN observers had left the port city
evidence_status: Contemporaneous foreign press report; flight extent explicitly unknown in the clipping
legal_status: No legal finding; the dispatch alone does not establish target selection, proportionality, or a war crime
scope_decision: Include reported bombing and displacement context; no fatalities or displaced-person total counted
limitations: Partial newspaper clipping; distinguish reported flight from verified displacement and do not infer casualty totals

event_name: Israeli aerial and artillery attacks in Gaza and refugee camps
location: Gaza city; Khan Yunis; Bureij; Rafah; Deir al-Balah
actor_as_reported: Israeli military (attributed by ICRC delegation as reported in peer-reviewed study)
event_categories: air and artillery bombardment; deaths and injuries in civilian/refugee locations
affected_people_or_estimate: About 190 killed and more than 400 wounded across six incidents, as reported by ICRC delegation; source excerpt does not disaggregate civilians and combatants
evidence_summary: Abu Sitta and Rempel report six intensive Israeli aerial and artillery bombing incidents in Gaza city and four refugee camps over six days, citing ICRC field reporting; the delegation head described the attacks as lacking military objectives
evidence_status: Secondary historical study based on ICRC records; strong contemporaneous institutional basis, original archival report not yet reviewed
legal_status: Potential distinction, proportionality, and civilian-protection violations warrant investigation; no criminal court finding identified
scope_decision: Include as a six-day incident series, not six fully documented individual rows; preserve ICRC-attributed totals and obtain original reports
limitations: The published summary gives combined deaths/injuries and omits individual incident breakdown and casualty status; reported no-military-objective characterization is the cited ICRC delegate's assessment

event_name: Capture and continued detention of Palestinian villagers
location: Near Tubas; Israeli detention camps
actor_as_reported: Israeli forces and authorities (UN observers / ICRC, as cited in study)
event_categories: capture; detention without due process; alleged arbitrary detention
affected_people_or_estimate: Two named villagers captured near Tubas in January; broader number not stated
evidence_summary: Peer-reviewed study cites UN truce observers' report that Israeli forces captured Ahmad Abd Abu Zaydi and Yusuf Hamid al-Fustuk while they worked their land near Tubas; it also quotes April ICRC mission head Jacques de Reynier that able-bodied men continued to be arrested and put in camps without due process
evidence_status: Secondary scholarship citing contemporaneous UN and ICRC records; named villagers' later fate not established here
legal_status: Potential arbitrary detention; no court finding in reviewed sources
scope_decision: Include detention pattern and named case lead; do not invent total detainees
limitations: Full UN observer and ICRC April reports not yet retrieved; study presents a broader argument about detention continuing after hostilities

event_name: Israeli settlement and repopulation on depopulated Palestinian land
location: Southern Israel and Galilee
actor_as_reported: Israeli Government and new Jewish settlers (as reported by New York Times)
event_categories: land takeover; settlement expansion; prevention of return context
affected_people_or_estimate: Nine settlements described as beginning in south after bulldozers cleared a wrecked Arab village; seven more reported started in Galilee; 51 planned
evidence_summary: Anne O'Hare McCormick reported rapid state resettlement on land left by Palestinians and characterized it as parallel to military occupation; she said this made refugee return unlikely
evidence_status: Contemporary foreign press account; records reported starts and plans rather than verified completion or legal title for each parcel
legal_status: Territorial/return implications require legal and property-record review; this row records expansion and displacement context, not a judicial legal finding
scope_decision: Include as expansionism evidence and reported state policy; keep settlement counts distinct from completed construction
limitations: NYT's 750000 refugee estimate is a broad conflict total, not an Israeli-attributed 1949 displacement count; land boundaries and individual village names need follow-up

event_name: Reported expulsion of Rameh residents
location: Rameh, Galilee
actor_as_reported: Israeli authorities (reported by an expelled resident)
event_categories: expulsion; displacement; alleged mistreatment
affected_people_or_estimate: 41 men reportedly expelled, including 28 Christians
evidence_summary: A short U.S. newspaper brief from Amman attributes the report to a deported Catholic resident who described Israeli authorities' treatment as intolerable
evidence_status: Contemporary foreign press report based on single witness account; independently uncorroborated in sources reviewed
legal_status: Potential forcible transfer; no legal finding
scope_decision: Include as a sourced allegation with low confidence pending corroboration; do not merge with annual displacement totals
limitations: Verify the witness identity, date and legal basis of expulsion; do not extrapolate beyond the 41 reported men

event_name: Refugee overcrowding in Egyptian-held southern Palestine
location: Gaza; Khan Yunis; Rafah; Deir al-Balah
actor_as_reported: Context: refugees in Egyptian-held area; not attributed as a discrete Israeli operation
event_categories: displacement context; camp overcrowding
affected_people_or_estimate: Egyptian Army representatives estimated 225000 refugees behind Egyptian lines: 70000 in Gaza and 95000 in Khan Yunis
evidence_summary: Associated Press field report describes crowded former barracks, prison cells, tents and caves, and records the Egyptian Army representatives' population estimates
evidence_status: Contemporaneous foreign press reporting; camp totals attributed to Egyptian Army representatives
legal_status: Not a separate Israeli crime finding and not counted as Israeli-attributed 1949 displacement
scope_decision: Include as humanitarian context only, explicitly outside Israel-attributed incident counts
limitations: Reported population is a stock estimate of refugees present, not a new displacement flow in 1949; AP dispatch reports Egyptian-held geography

event_name: El Auja Bedouin roundup and expulsion
location: El Auja demilitarized zone and Negev; across Egypt border
actor_as_reported: Israeli military
event_categories: military roundup; forced cross-border expulsion; deaths reported; destruction of tents crops and possessions
affected_people_or_estimate: About 4,000 Bedouins expelled by 2 September; 13 deaths reported in statements collected by the Mixed Armistice Commission investigation
evidence_summary: UNTSO Chief of Staff Riley transmitted the 6 September commission investigation: five tribes' representatives said Israeli operations to clear the area began 20 August, used troops armored cars and reconnaissance aircraft, expelled the group into Egypt, and burned tents crops and possessions; they reported 13 Bedouin killed
evidence_status: UN truce-supervision report documents roundup and expulsion; 13-death figure is testimony relayed by the investigation; Israel denied entering the demilitarized zone and said El Auja residents followed expelled Bedouins, describing the group as infiltrators
legal_status: Potential forcible transfer, civilian-protection and armistice violations warrant investigation; no criminal court finding
scope_decision: Include Israeli military conduct and clearly state the disagreement over zone entry and death attribution
limitations: UN report says approximately 4,000 by 2 September; separate roughly 1,000 Arab expulsions since March are reported in same document and may overlap; do not sum without case-level reconciliation

event_name: Transfer/expulsion of Palestinian Arab residents from Majdal to Gaza
location: Majdal (Migdal Gad/Ashkelon) to Gaza
actor_as_reported: Israeli authorities
event_categories: expulsion or coerced transfer; displacement; continued settlement/repopulation context
affected_people_or_estimate: UN commission later records about 2,000 Arabs expelled; JTA reports final 75 families transferred by 15 October
evidence_summary: JTA contemporaneously reported completion of the transfer of the last 75 Arab families from Migdal Gad to Gaza; UN Mixed Armistice Commission report in 1951 records about 2,000 Arabs expelled by Israeli authorities and directed repatriation/restoration for those deemed entitled
evidence_status: Contemporary foreign press confirms transfer; subsequent UN commission characterizes it as expulsion; Israeli account and family reunification rationale should be checked against full proceedings
legal_status: Potential forcible transfer and property/restoration issues; UN commission action is not a criminal judgment
scope_decision: Include with contemporaneous and later UN evidence; preserve ambiguity about consent and population scope
limitations: About 2,000 is the commission's case estimate; 75 families is the last group reported, not the total displaced; avoid implying exact date or that all 2,000 were sent in October

event_name: Reported uprooting and land confiscation in Wadi Ara villages
location: Wadi Ara, Triangle region
actor_as_reported: Israeli authorities (attribution from historical context; contemporary press claim requires original article review)
event_categories: reported forced displacement; village uprooting; land confiscation
affected_people_or_estimate: Residents of 13 small villages; number of people not stated
evidence_summary: Adel Manna cites the contemporary Palestinian newspaper Al-Ittihad (10 February 1951), which reported that inhabitants of thirteen small villages in Wadi Ara were uprooted and their lands confiscated; a 1984 UN Special Committee report likewise records the expulsion and confiscation
evidence_status: Contemporary Palestinian press report accessed through peer-reviewed historical scholarship, with later UN corroboration; original Arabic article not yet reviewed
legal_status: Potential forcible transfer and property seizure; no criminal judgment identified
scope_decision: Include as a documented lead with population count unknown; verify village names and individual orders before annual totals
limitations: Do not estimate displaced persons from village count; later UN report's framing and underlying sources need review; attribution to Israeli authorities is contextual pending direct text

event_name: Jordanian complaints of Israeli-force attacks on border villages
location: Beit Iksa; Beit Surik; Yalu; Saffa; Sharafat; Falam; Deir Ballut; Imwas
actor_as_reported: Israeli armed forces (as alleged in complaints listed by UNTSO)
event_categories: reported village attacks; shootings; civilian deaths; home destruction
affected_people_or_estimate: Jordanian complaints listed two civilians killed in Saffa, ten killed and eight wounded in Sharafat, and one man and two children killed in Falam; other complaints give no casualty count
evidence_summary: UNTSO report S/2048 lists Jordanian complaints alleging Israeli-force attacks on multiple villages between late January and mid-February. The Mixed Armistice Commission later condemned wanton killings and home destruction collectively, but said the complaints had been acted upon without adjudicating each listed claim separately
evidence_status: Contemporaneous UN record of complaints and a collective commission response; individual allegations not separately verified in the cited report
legal_status: Potential unlawful attacks and killings; commission resolution is armistice oversight, not a criminal judgment
scope_decision: Include only alleged Israeli actions; do not record Arab-party complaints as incidents or sum reported deaths as a confirmed toll
limitations: Jordanian complaint figures; no event-level investigation results given in this section; preserve reported versus confirmed status and avoid treating the 23 fatality claims as verified aggregate

event_name: Israeli-force shelling of Idna
location: Idna, Hebron area
actor_as_reported: Israeli forces
event_categories: artillery or mortar shelling; truce violation
affected_people_or_estimate: No casualty number in the cited Commission finding
evidence_summary: The Jordan-Israel Mixed Armistice Commission found shelling by Israeli forces constituted a technical violation of the General Armistice Agreement and condemned it; the same decision stated the violation resulted from lesser contraventions by Jordanian residents
evidence_status: Contemporaneous UN armistice finding; precise weapon and casualties are not established in the quoted decision
legal_status: Formal armistice violation finding; not a criminal court determination
scope_decision: Include the Israeli force action and preserve the Commission's causal/context qualification
limitations: The Commission said demarcation lines were not clearly marked and ordered ground marking and local telephone links; no casualty tally supplied

event_name: Beit Jala-area raid
location: Outskirts of Beit Jala, Bethlehem area, then Jordan-controlled territory
actor_as_reported: Armed Israeli group (as reported to UNTSO; IDF or other state chain of command not established)
event_categories: house demolition by explosives; armed attack; civilian deaths and injuries
affected_people_or_estimate: UNTSO report records six Jordanians killed and three seriously wounded; Palestinian retrospective account identifies Palestinian civilian victims including two children
evidence_summary: Jordan reported that armed Israelis penetrated Jordan-controlled territory and blew up houses. Leaflets at the scene attributed the act to Israelis and linked it to an unsolved killing in Israel. The Mixed Armistice Commission unanimously found a serious breach of Article III(2), expressed horror, and called on Israel’s delegation to prevent recurrence.
evidence_status: Contemporaneous UN record with unanimous armistice finding; reported victim count not a criminal adjudication or proof of military command
legal_status: Formal serious armistice breach finding; no criminal court judgment identified
scope_decision: Include as an attributed armed-Israeli lead; exclude from confirmed Israeli military/state-actor subtotal unless command or official link is established
limitations: UNTSO identifies armed Israelis but not an IDF unit or official chain of command. Use six killed/three seriously wounded as the UN tally; Palestinian archive repeats it and adds detail from other sources, not independent verification.

event_name: Qaffin-area house bombing
location: Near Qaffin village, then Jordan-controlled territory
actor_as_reported: Perpetrator group not conclusively identified; UN report notes scene leaflets and penetration into Jordan-controlled territory, but no military affiliation is established
event_categories: house bombing; civilian deaths; alleged reprisal
affected_people_or_estimate: One woman and four children aged 1–15 killed; no wounded total given
evidence_summary: Jordan alleged a house had been blown up, apparently as reprisal for the killing of an Israeli woman. The UN report says leaflets were found and the perpetrators had penetrated about five kilometres into Jordan-controlled territory. The Commission, with the Jordan delegation and chair voting in favour and the Israeli delegate abstaining, considered it a breach of Article IV(3) and called on Israeli authorities to prevent such acts.
evidence_status: Contemporaneous UN report of Jordan’s complaint and a Mixed Armistice Commission decision; perpetrator identity and command chain remain unresolved
legal_status: Commission armistice-breach finding; not a criminal judgment
scope_decision: Retain as an Israeli-linked attribution lead under review; do not count as proven military, settler, or state operation without perpetrator identification
limitations: Report says 'similar charge' and notes leaflets/penetration but does not expressly establish IDF involvement; exact bombing date is not stated, so month and Commission reporting date are used.

event_name: Es Sani Bedouin forced-transfer and temporary displacement
location: Beersheba area to Jordan-controlled territory; proposed internal relocation within Israel-controlled territory
actor_as_reported: Israeli-controlled authorities (the UN investigation describes a forced transfer inside Israel-controlled territory; individual officials/order not identified)
event_categories: coercive relocation; temporary cross-border displacement; threatened land transfer
affected_people_or_estimate: Approximately 800 Es Sani Bedouins crossed into Jordan to escape a forced transfer to less desirable land within Israel-controlled territory; a negotiated arrangement later returned them to Israel
evidence_summary: The Jordanian complaint alleged expulsion from the Beersheba area. The UN investigation indicated that the group crossed into Jordan to escape a forced internal transfer; at Jordan’s request, an arrangement was made to return those who crossed to Israel. The report says the matter appeared closed after return arrangements.
evidence_status: Contemporaneous UN investigation; approximately 800 is a reported group size, not a verified annual net displacement count
legal_status: No criminal or court finding identified; evidence documents coercive transfer pressure and temporary flight
scope_decision: Include as an Israeli-controlled-authority displacement episode; record approximately 800 affected, but do not label all 800 as permanently expelled or add them to an annual net total
limitations: UN report does not name the official who ordered relocation, provide individual records, or say how many returned; approximate count comes from the complaint.

event_name: Wadi Ara / Kafr Ara border-area shooting
location: Near Ayn al-Sahla, Wadi Ara, Israel side of the Jordan armistice line
actor_as_reported: Israeli soldiers / Border Police (source terminology varies)
event_categories: shooting of civilians; deaths and injuries
affected_people_or_estimate: Two killed and five wounded, including children, according to later archival studies
evidence_summary: Adel Manna’s study says villagers approached the border for customary Eid al-Fitr visits and Israeli soldiers opened fire on 23 June without warning; it reports an internal committee later characterized the shooting as an unpremeditated error and no criminal offense. Zaki Shalom’s study, drawing on Israeli government records, dates it 25 June, reports the same toll, and preserves the IDF claim of an order and warning as well as civilian/political objections. The exact date remains disputed pending original minutes and contemporary press.
evidence_status: Later archival scholarship with conflicting dates and competing accounts; casualty count consistent across sources; no contemporaneous non-Israeli newspaper report yet located
legal_status: Internal committee reportedly concluded soldiers committed no criminal offense; no independent court judgment identified in reviewed sources
scope_decision: Include as an Israeli military/police action with date disputed; retain the Palestinian civilian account and official defense, without turning the incident into a legal verdict
limitations: Manna dates the event 23 June 1952; Shalom dates it 25 June. Verify against cited committee minutes and contemporaneous press before choosing a single day. The works are later scholarship, not non-Israeli contemporary reporting.

event_name: Attack on Bedouin camp near El Berig
location: Near Wadi Gaza and El Berig refugee camp, Egyptian-controlled Gaza Strip
actor_as_reported: Armed Israelis (UN observer reported a group crossing the demarcation line; state command not established)
event_categories: armed raid; shooting; explosive attack; killings and injuries; tent and water-pump destruction; hospital fire
affected_people_or_estimate: UN observer report lists 7 killed (3 men, 1 woman, 2 boys and 1 girl) and 12 wounded; Egyptian complaint initially listed 6 killed and 9 seriously injured, noting one woman later died. Eight tents were destroyed or damaged; water pump and pump house destroyed.
evidence_summary: An Egyptian-Israeli Mixed Armistice Commission complaint alleged an armed Israeli force crossed the demarcation line, attacked sleeping residents and fired near a tuberculosis hospital. A UN military observer visited the site and recorded armed Israelis crossing the line, the 7/12 casualty list, damaged tents and water system, and rounds striking the hospital. The observer reported tracks crossing the line in both directions.
evidence_status: Contemporaneous UN observer inspection embedded in an Egyptian-submitted Security Council document; event-specific casualty discrepancy between the complaint and observer report preserved
legal_status: No criminal court finding identified; armistice complaint and field observations are not a criminal judgment
scope_decision: Include as an Israeli-armed-group lead supported by UN observer material; do not label an IDF operation without command evidence
limitations: Observer casualty tally differs from the initial Egyptian complaint; the source describes armed Israelis but does not identify a unit or command order. No displaced-person total supplied.

event_name: Killing of Salem brothers after field detention
location: Near the Egypt-Gaza armistice demarcation line, Gaza Strip
actor_as_reported: Armed Israelis (UN observer found six crossed from Israel; military unit affiliation not stated)
event_categories: abduction; shooting of civilians; killing; alleged close-range execution
affected_people_or_estimate: Two Palestinian brothers, Salem Hussein Salem (24) and Mohammed Hussein Salem (28), killed; their father and young daughter were released.
evidence_summary: Egyptian authorities complained that Israeli soldiers crossed the line, detained a man, his two sons and a young girl, released the father and daughter, and killed the sons. A UN military observer investigated the same day and reported six armed Israelis crossed the line, forced the family toward it, then shot the two brothers. Tracks, bloodspots and cartridge cases supported the account; the observer described point-blank gunfire and bayonet wounds.
evidence_status: Contemporaneous UN observer investigation of a party complaint; physical evidence and the scene were recorded, but no judicial proceeding is cited
legal_status: Potential unlawful killing and treatment of civilians; no criminal judgment identified
scope_decision: Include as an attributed armed-Israeli incident; the UN observer did not identify a specific unit or chain of command
limitations: Victim spellings vary within the UN document; preserve source spellings in future person-level work. The record gives no independent court or prosecution finding.

event_name: Killing of Hussein Gaber Ibrahim
location: Agricultural field in Egyptian-controlled Gaza Strip, about 600 metres west of the armistice line
actor_as_reported: Shooter unidentified; Egyptian complaint alleged armed Israelis, and UN observer found Israeli-marked ammunition but no eyewitness
event_categories: shooting of a farmer; death; possible extrajudicial killing
affected_people_or_estimate: One Palestinian man, Hussein Gaber Ibrahim, killed.
evidence_summary: An Egyptian complaint alleged armed Israelis crossed the demarcation line and killed Ibrahim while he worked his land. A UN observer inspected the body and scene the same day, documented blood traces and bullets consistent with a prone victim, and found cartridge cases bearing Israeli markings. The observer explicitly noted there were no eyewitnesses.
evidence_status: Contemporaneous UN observer inspection supports the killing and Israeli-marked ammunition; attribution to an individual or unit remains unproved
legal_status: No criminal or armistice adjudication identified in the inspected passage
scope_decision: Keep as an attribution lead; do not count as a confirmed Israeli perpetrator incident until the shooter is identified
limitations: No eyewitness to the killing; Israeli-marked cartridge cases are material evidence but do not identify a shooter or unit. No displaced-person figure.

event_name: Israeli military attacks on Falameh and Rantis
location: Falameh and Rantis, then Jordan-controlled West Bank
actor_as_reported: Israeli military forces
event_categories: cross-border raid; village attack; house demolition; civilian and National Guard deaths/injuries; armistice violations
affected_people_or_estimate: At least 3 Arabs killed and 10–12 wounded in incomplete information reported by the UK Foreign Secretary; the source does not give a final verified count. UNTSO records additional attacks and house destruction.
evidence_summary: UNTSO reported Israeli military forces crossing the demarcation line in attacks on Falameh and Rantis in January. In the House of Commons, the UK Foreign Secretary said the Mixed Armistice Commission majority held Israel responsible for armistice breaches; he reported at least three killed and 10 or 12 wounded, while expressly saying the casualty details were incomplete. The questioner's claim of at least ten deaths was not confirmed in the minister's answer.
evidence_status: Contemporaneous UNTSO/MAC record and independent non-Israeli parliamentary account; casualty total remains provisional and reported counts differ
legal_status: MAC majority held Israel responsible for armistice breaches; no criminal judgment identified
scope_decision: Include Israeli military actions and preserve the provisional casualty count; do not convert the parliamentary estimate into a verified final toll
limitations: Dates include a 22/23 January Falameh attack and the 28–29 January raids; source descriptions and casualty figures do not fully align. Verify individual village and victim totals against full MAC investigation reports.

event_name: Raid on Bureij refugee camp
location: Bureij refugee camp, Gaza Strip
actor_as_reported: Armed Israelis (UNTSO/MAC majority attribution; UNRWA described armed raiders)
event_categories: armed attack on refugee camp; civilian deaths and injuries; displacement
affected_people_or_estimate: UNRWA reported 20 refugees killed, 27 seriously wounded and 35 less serious casualties. More than 1,800 refugees fled Bureij to other camps; temporary flight, not a confirmed permanent displacement total.
evidence_summary: UNRWA's acting director reported that bombs were thrown into huts while refugees slept and gunfire hit people fleeing; he called the attack apparently premeditated and indiscriminate. The UNTSO Chief of Staff reported that the Commission majority found the raid was carried out by a group of armed Israelis; the exact motive was described as a likely reprisal, not conclusively established.
evidence_status: Contemporaneous UNRWA impact report and UNTSO/MAC attribution; casualty and displacement figures are source-reported
legal_status: No criminal court judgment identified; UN Secretary-General/UNTSO condemned the attack and MAC majority attributed it to armed Israelis
scope_decision: Include as an Israeli-attributed attack on a refugee camp; record >1,800 as temporary flight, not permanent or net displacement
limitations: UNRWA counts distinguish 27 seriously wounded from 35 less serious casualties. The more than 1,800 who left were reported as seeking shelter in other camps after the raid; their return timing is not established here.

event_name: Qibya raid
location: Qibya, Shuqba and Budrus, then Jordan-controlled West Bank
actor_as_reported: Israeli regular army / armed forces
event_categories: cross-border military raid; home and school destruction; shelling; civilian deaths and injuries; armistice violation
affected_people_or_estimate: UNTSO investigation recorded 42 killed and 15 wounded at Qibya, with 41 houses and a school destroyed. Jordan's 16 October letter reported 42 recovered bodies and said more might remain under wreckage. No reliable displacement total was found.
evidence_summary: UNTSO reported roughly half a battalion of Israel's regular army crossed the demarcation line, attacked Qibya, and part of the force entered Shuqba; supporting Israeli forces shelled Budrus. The Mixed Armistice Commission condemned the regular army action. Security Council Resolution 101 found the retaliatory action violated cease-fire provisions and was inconsistent with the Armistice Agreement and Charter obligations. The alleged trigger of the attack remained unverified by the UNTSO investigation.
evidence_status: Contemporaneous UNTSO investigation, MAC finding, Security Council resolution, and Jordan's complaint; preserve count and source differences
legal_status: Security Council found cease-fire/Armistice/Charter violations; no criminal court judgment or individual criminal finding identified
scope_decision: Include as an Israeli regular-army operation; use the UNTSO count and preserve the Jordanian complaint as a separate count source
limitations: UNTSO's 42 dead/15 wounded is a contemporaneous investigated count, not necessarily a final historical total. Jordan reported 42 bodies recovered and additional possible victims under rubble. The UNTSO report found no evidence establishing who committed the alleged triggering murder in Israel.

event_name: Nahalin night raid
location: Nahalin, Bethlehem district, then Jordan-controlled West Bank
actor_as_reported: Armed Israeli group (UNTSO/Mixed Armistice Commission investigation attributed the attack to militarily trained Israelis and condemned Israel; regular-unit chain not specified)
event_categories: armed night raid; firing and explosive entry; killings and injuries; house and mosque damage; armistice breach
affected_people_or_estimate: UNTSO/MAC account: 9 killed (5 National Guards, 1 woman in the village, 3 Arab Legionnaires in a reinforcement vehicle); 14 villagers wounded, plus an officer and 4 Legionnaires wounded. Seven houses and the mosque were damaged. No displacement count given. Jordan's initial complaint said 18 civilians wounded; JTA's early report said 10 killed and 16 wounded.
evidence_summary: Jordan reported an armed raid shortly after midnight. UN observers inspected damaged houses and the mosque, interviewed wounded people and witnesses, and traced footprints from the village toward the demarcation line and similar tracks on the Israeli side. Witnesses reported attackers using non-Arab words including a Hebrew command. The Mixed Armistice Commission adopted a resolution condemning Israel; its chair said the evidence established guilt without question. JTA's first-day report carried preliminary casualty figures before UNTSO's later breakdown.
evidence_status: Contemporaneous UNTSO field investigation and MAC resolution, with a separate contemporaneous JTA report; preserve differing preliminary casualty figures
legal_status: MAC found a flagrant armistice breach and condemned Israel; no criminal court verdict identified
scope_decision: Include as an Israeli-attributed armed raid; keep the UN casualty breakdown distinct from the Jordanian complaint and early JTA figures
limitations: UNTSO reports 14 villagers wounded and additional military casualties; Jordan's initial complaint says 18 civilians wounded, and JTA initially reported 16 wounded/10 deaths. Do not add these totals. No annual displacement figure.

event_name: Israeli army raid east of Gaza (Operation Black Arrow)
location: Egyptian military camp and civilian infrastructure east of Gaza, Egyptian-controlled Gaza Strip
actor_as_reported: Israeli regular army forces; Mixed Armistice Commission found the operation planned and ordered by Israeli authorities
event_categories: cross-border army raid; attack on military camp; civilian deaths and injuries; damage to railway and water infrastructure; armistice breach
affected_people_or_estimate: MAC count: 36 Egyptian military killed and 2 civilians killed; 29 military wounded and 2 civilians wounded. Egypt's initial complaint reported 37 military and 2 civilians killed, 30 military and 2 civilians wounded. UNTSO identifies one civilian killed as a 7-year-old Palestinian boy.
evidence_summary: UNTSO investigation found Israeli forces crossed the demarcation line east of Gaza, attacked an Egyptian camp and two civilian structures (stationmaster's house and a water-pump house). The Commission characterized it as prearranged and planned and ordered by Israeli authorities. The UN recorded the two civilians killed and two wounded separately from military casualties; the Security Council condemned the attack.
evidence_status: Contemporaneous UNTSO/MAC findings and Security Council action; military and civilian counts separated; one Palestinian child victim identified
legal_status: Security Council condemned the attack as a cease-fire and Armistice Agreement/Charter violation; no criminal court judgment identified
scope_decision: Include as an Israeli state military operation; distinguish attack on military camp from harm to civilian homes/infrastructure and Palestinian civilians
limitations: Egypt's initial complaint and MAC figures differ slightly for military casualties. Civilian identities beyond the boy are not established in the sources summarized here. No displacement count found.

event_name: Israeli patrol shooting and abduction of Hassan Abu Anza
location: Abbassan area, Gaza Strip
actor_as_reported: Israeli patrol and two armed Israelis (as found by Mixed Armistice Commission)
event_categories: shooting and wounding of unarmed Palestinian farmer; cross-border entry; removal of wounded victim
affected_people_or_estimate: Hassan Abu Anza wounded while planting watermelons; his donkey was also taken; no other casualties or displacement figures reported.
evidence_summary: A UN-observed Mixed Armistice Commission decision found that an Israeli patrol fired across the demarcation line at an unarmed farmer in Egyptian-controlled territory. Two armed Israelis crossed and removed the wounded farmer and his donkey to Israeli-controlled territory. The Commission voted to find a flagrant violation and requested his return.
evidence_status: Contemporaneous UN observer/MAC finding
legal_status: Commission found a flagrant General Armistice Agreement violation; not a criminal court judgment
scope_decision: Include as a specifically identified Palestinian civilian victim and an Israeli-attributed act
limitations: The Commission resolution establishes the reported firing, wounding and removal, but no later disposition or return record is included in this source.

event_name: Israeli shelling of Gaza and Deir el Balla
location: Gaza city and Deir el Balla village, Gaza Strip
actor_as_reported: Israeli forces (UNTSO updates as relayed in U.S. diplomatic record)
event_categories: mortar and artillery shelling of civilian areas; civilian deaths and injuries; reported harm to children
affected_people_or_estimate: Latest update relayed by U.S. diplomat reported 55 civilians killed and 102 wounded, including an earlier Egyptian claim that 17 children were killed; one Egyptian soldier killed and four wounded. Initial figures in the April 5 telegram were explicitly unconfirmed.
evidence_summary: UN observers recorded multiple artillery/mortar impacts in Deir el Balla and Gaza town on 5 April. The diplomat's 6 April update relayed the latest figures (55 civilians killed, 102 wounded) and said firing on civilians appeared to be the largest such attack since Qibya; the cited record does not provide a final incident-specific finding or criminal inquiry.
evidence_status: Contemporaneous U.S. diplomatic record relaying UNTSO observations and evolving Egyptian casualty figures; distinguish initial unconfirmed totals from the later update
legal_status: No criminal court or definitive final casualty determination identified in the reviewed record; civilian-targeting concerns require investigation
scope_decision: Include as a reported Israeli shelling incident with provisional casualty figures attributed to the 6 April diplomatic update; do not present the earlier 42/102 total as confirmed
limitations: The 42 dead/102 wounded report in the 5 April telegram was explicitly unconfirmed; the 55 dead/102 wounded figure appears in a later 6 April update relayed through the same diplomatic record. The sources do not provide an annual displacement count.

event_name: Khan Yunis raid and Bani Suheila machine-gunning
location: Khan Yunis and Bani Suheila, Gaza Strip
actor_as_reported: Israeli light-armoured military unit
event_categories: police-station demolition; damage to hospital under construction; machine-gunning of residential buildings; attack on Egyptian position; deaths and injuries
affected_people_or_estimate: UNTSO reported Egyptian-authority tally of 36 killed and 13 wounded across police, armed forces and civilians; exact count not established and observers saw few listed victims. A contemporary on-scene NYT report separately counted 8 villagers killed (within 35 total deaths). No displacement figure established.
evidence_summary: UNTSO reported that an Israeli light-armoured unit entered Egyptian-controlled territory, machine-gunned and demolished the Khan Yunis police station, partly destroyed a hospital under construction, machine-gunned buildings and homes in Bani Suheila, and attacked an Egyptian position. A contemporaneous on-scene NYT report, republished by Covering Palestine, identified eight villagers among 35 deaths, 15 policemen and 12 Palestinian Arab soldiers; its headline said 39. Keep these source counts separate; no reliable Palestinian civilian-only total or displacement count is established.
evidence_status: Contemporaneous UNTSO account with an incomplete investigation and a separate on-scene foreign press report; casualty counts differ and their scopes are not identical
legal_status: No criminal court judgment identified; record the attack and reported impact without a legal conclusion
scope_decision: Include as an Israeli military attack affecting a Palestinian town; keep civilian, police, and military subgroups distinct and retain the UN's uncertainty
limitations: The UNTSO report said exact casualties were not established and observers saw few listed victims. Egypt's 36/13 count includes civilians, police and armed forces. NYT headline/body totals conflict. No measured displacement count.

event_name: Israeli military occupation and administration of Gaza Strip
location: Gaza Strip
actor_as_reported: Israeli armed forces and military administration
event_categories: military occupation; curfew; screening and interrogation detention; interruption of UNRWA relief; proposed refugee resettlement/territorial consolidation
affected_people_or_estimate: More than 213,000 registered/ration-recipient refugees were in Gaza (population stock, not new displacement). Large numbers were taken to interrogation centres during screening, but no detainee count was supplied. No defensible 1956 displacement-flow count was identified.
evidence_summary: UNRWA reported Israeli military occupation following the 1 November attack, curfew preventing usual ration distribution, restricted movement of UNTSO observers, widespread screening and large numbers taken to interrogation centres, and interruption/reorganization of services. A UN Secretary-General representative later noted administrative measures that appeared to facilitate permanence of the situation achieved by military action. Historical scholarship documents proposals to resettle Gaza refugees outside the Strip; those were proposals, not proof of completed transfers.
evidence_status: Contemporaneous UNRWA and UN reporting, supplemented by peer-reviewed archival research; refugee-death lists are tracked in separate Khan Yunis and Rafah entries.
legal_status: UN General Assembly demanded withdrawal of Israeli forces from Egyptian territory; possible permanence/transfer plans require separate legal assessment. No criminal judgment on this occupation episode in the reviewed sources.
scope_decision: Include Israeli occupation, detention/screening practices and territorial policy; do not count pre-existing refugees as newly displaced and do not report unexecuted resettlement proposals as completed expulsions.
limitations: UNRWA's 213,000 is a population stock. Agency reports list 66 other alleged November deaths (48 refugees) beyond the Khan Yunis and Rafah lists; individual deaths were not verified and categories are not added here. No annual displaced-person count found.

event_name: Killing of civilians during occupation of Khan Yunis
location: Khan Yunis town and adjacent UNRWA refugee camp, Gaza Strip
actor_as_reported: Israeli troops
event_categories: occupation; shootings during search/screening operation; civilian killings
affected_people_or_estimate: UNRWA received lists from sources it considered trustworthy naming 275 people allegedly killed: 140 refugees and 135 local residents. Exact number of dead and wounded was unknown; list could not be individually verified.
evidence_summary: UNRWA reported Israeli troops occupied Khan Yunis and the adjacent camp on 3 November. Israeli authorities said there had been resistance and Palestinian refugees participated; refugees said resistance had ceased and unarmed civilians were killed as troops searched for men with arms. The Agency relied on limited sources, including eyewitness accounts by UNRWA employees.
evidence_status: Contemporaneous UNRWA report with listed names and eyewitness sources; deaths alleged and individual records not verified; accounts of resistance conflict.
legal_status: No criminal-court finding identified in the reviewed record; preserve the allegation and UNRWA's evidence limits.
scope_decision: Include as a Palestinian civilian/refugee casualty lead, with the named-list total explicitly qualified and separated by population category.
limitations: The 275 is not a final verified death toll and includes local residents and refugees; it must not be combined with Rafah or the separate 66-name list without person-level reconciliation.

event_name: Rafah refugee-camp screening shooting
location: Rafah refugee camp, Gaza Strip
actor_as_reported: Israeli occupying forces / soldiers
event_categories: mass screening; shooting of crowd; civilian killings and injuries
affected_people_or_estimate: UNRWA received lists from sources it considered trustworthy naming 111 people allegedly killed: 103 refugees, 7 local residents and 1 Egyptian. Individual deaths and wounded totals could not be verified; camp population exceeded 32,000 refugees.
evidence_summary: UNRWA says both Israeli authorities and its own sources agreed refugees were killed and wounded by occupying forces during a screening operation. Israeli authorities said refugees were hostile and resisted; refugees denied resistance. UNRWA's account states the announcement did not reach some sections, insufficient time was allowed to reach screening points, and some soldiers apparently panicked and fired on a running crowd.
evidence_status: Contemporaneous UNRWA report; named-list count based on sources considered trustworthy, but not every death verified and the full list of dead or missing could not be completed.
legal_status: No criminal-court finding identified in the reviewed record; UNRWA protested to Israel and requested steps to prevent recurrence.
scope_decision: Include the operation and affected Palestinians; mark 111 as a reported list, not an independently verified final toll.
limitations: The 111 includes 103 refugees, seven local residents and one Egyptian. Do not add the 66 other listed November deaths; UNRWA said individual deaths remained unverified. No displacement flow count found.

event_name: Kafr Qasim curfew killings
location: Kafr Qasim, within Israel; Palestinian citizen community
actor_as_reported: Israeli Border Police; Colonel Issachar Shadmi issued the curfew order; Major Shmuel Malinki led the unit; eight Border Police were convicted of murder for 43 deaths
event_categories: imposition of curfew with very short notice; shooting of unarmed civilians returning from work; killings of men, women and children
affected_people_or_estimate: Contemporary report at disclosure stated men, women and children were killed but gave no count. Later court and news reports distinguish 43 deaths in the murder convictions, at least 47 shot dead, and a 49-person community total; keep counts tied to the source and counting method.
evidence_summary: An AP report disclosed the killings on 12 December 1956, 45 days after the event, reporting that Israeli authorities said frontier police had killed Arab villagers during curfew. A 1958 JTA report on the military tribunal states eight Border Police were convicted of murder in 43 deaths and the court called Shadmi's order 'manifestly illegal'; it said Malinki should have refused the order. JTA's 1959 report gives 49 killed and says Shadmi was fined for acting beyond authority but acquitted of murder.
evidence_status: Contemporary foreign press at official disclosure and contemporary reports of criminal proceedings; victims were Palestinian citizens of Israel, not refugees or residents of occupied territory.
legal_status: Military court convicted Border Police officers of murder in 43 deaths and held the order manifestly illegal; Shadmi's separate prosecution ended in acquittal on murder and a token fine for exceeding authority.
scope_decision: Include as a documented Israeli state-force killing of Palestinians; preserve the counts from disclosure, convictions and broader community toll separately.
limitations: Censorship delayed public reporting. The legal conviction count (43) and later total of 49 are not interchangeable; exact breakdown of deaths beyond the convictions needs court-record reconciliation. No displaced-person count.

event_name: Israeli army attack in Husan, Wadi Fukin, Sharafa and Khader
location: Jordanian-administered West Bank, south of Jerusalem
actor_as_reported: Israeli regular army
event_categories: cross-border military raid; attack on National Guard detachments and police post; school demolition; shelling of villages; civilian deaths and injuries
affected_people_or_estimate: Mixed Armistice Commission records 12 National Guards killed near Husan, two civilians wounded there, school demolished at Wadi Fukin, 25 Jordanians killed and six wounded at Sharafa, and a 12-year-old girl killed and three civilians wounded at Khader. Jordan's complaint reported 25 killed and six wounded across the area, including civilians/children; UK Hansard later cited about 39 killed.
evidence_summary: The Commission majority found large Israeli regular army forces launched a major, unprovoked and premeditated attack, using infantry, armored vehicles, artillery and aircraft. It separately documented actions at Husan, Wadi Fukin, Sharafa and Khader and condemned Israel for a flagrant armistice-agreement aggression. Jordan's complaint and later UK parliamentary summary give different aggregates.
evidence_status: Contemporaneous UNTSO/MAC findings, Jordan complaint and British parliamentary account; casualties are split by location and category where possible; differing totals preserved.
legal_status: Mixed Armistice Commission condemned the attack as a flagrant violation of the Jordan-Israel General Armistice Agreement; not a criminal trial.
scope_decision: Include Israeli military action; do not present the full Jordanian military/police toll as Palestinian civilian casualties.
limitations: Jordan's aggregate of 25 and Hansard's approximate 39 differ from the detailed UN/MAC outcome, which identifies multiple attacked localities. No displacement total supplied.

event_name: Israeli army raid on Qalqiliya police post and town
location: Qalqiliya, Jordanian-administered West Bank
actor_as_reported: Israeli army forces
event_categories: military raid; bombardment of town; demolition of police post and water pumping house; home and school damage; civilian deaths and injuries
affected_people_or_estimate: UN observers saw 48 Jordanian dead: 43 army, National Guard and police; 3 civilians; 2 unidentified. Israel reported 18 members of its forces killed. UN observers documented one child killed and several family members wounded by a shell at a home; women, civilians and forces' category details should not be combined beyond the report's 48-person breakdown.
evidence_summary: UNTSO investigated the day after the Israeli attack. It recorded Israeli forces entering and demolishing the police post, destruction of the adjacent water pumping house, shelling and severe damage to homes and the school, and 48 bodies. The Mixed Armistice Commission meeting on Jordan's complaint was not completed; Israel's delegation was absent. A contemporary JTA report covered the raid; the UN Chief of Staff criticized Israel's unilateral investigation and retaliatory action without UN verification.
evidence_status: Contemporaneous UN observer investigation plus contemporary foreign press; casualty total includes military, police, civilian and unidentified victims.
legal_status: UNTSO record documents actions and casualty observations; no completed MAC adjudication or criminal court finding identified for this attack.
scope_decision: Include Israeli military action and clearly separate civilian and military losses; do not present 48 as civilian deaths.
limitations: The total 48 includes 43 armed-service/police, three civilians and two unidentified; Israeli reported casualties are a separate party total. The UN investigation and Jordan complaint did not result in a completed MAC adjudication. No displacement count found.

event_name: Israeli afforestation and land preparation in Government House neutral zone
location: Government House / Jebel el Mukabber area Jerusalem
actor_as_reported: Israeli laborers protected by Israeli Border Police; Israel said afforestation/beautification
event_categories: land-use expansion; road cutting; ploughing; olive-tree removal; armed protection; contested neutral-zone status
affected_people_or_estimate: No people reported killed wounded detained or displaced; UNTSO noted 50–60 olive trees uprooted but ownership required title search; zone appeared predominantly Arab-owned in UNCCP records
evidence_summary: UNTSO reported laborers staked out land on 21 July then cut roads and ploughed; observed up to about 15 armed Israeli Border Police protecting laborers and no Israeli military except officers inspecting twice; Israel had progressively extended cultivation since 1949. UNTSO could not authoritatively rule on land-use claims. Jordan alleged armed positions and fencing; these remain attributed allegations. UNTSO also documented Jordanian military presence/traffic.
evidence_status: UNTSO confirms work armed police protection uprooted trees and prior cultivation expansion; specific ownership unresolved; no authoritative ruling on civilian land-use dispute
legal_status: No criminal judgment. UNTSO recommended suspending project pending negotiations and respecting ownership established by registry search; Security Council Resolution 127 (1958) later addressed civilian use and title.
scope_decision: Include as land-use/expansion evidence with contested-status framing; not verified displacement or war-crime finding
limitations: Specific parcel and tree ownership were not established without title search. No displacement casualty or detention total reported. New Yorker report says 25 families were removed during Gaza withdrawal; circumstances and voluntariness remain unverified. Resolution 127 is 1958 follow-up not 1957 finding.

event_name: Reported deportation of al-Syajj Arabs
location: al-Syajj, Negev (Naqab)
actor_as_reported: Israeli authorities (as reported in Palestinian scholarship)
event_categories: deportation; forced displacement
affected_people_or_estimate: Number of people and destination not stated
evidence_summary: Nihad Boqa’i's 2008 Palestinian-Israel Journal article states in an endnote that Israel deported al-Syajj Arabs in the Negev in 1957; the note cites Hillel Cohen (2001) and Wakim Wakim (2001).
evidence_status: Secondary Palestinian scholarship citing earlier research; underlying sources not yet reviewed
legal_status: Potential forced transfer; no legal determination identified
scope_decision: Include as a sourced displacement lead; do not infer a count, date, operation or destination
limitations: The endnote gives only the year and community name. Verify Cohen, Wakim and archival/community records before treating details as established; no annual displacement total can be derived.

event_name: Issawiya road closure and police shooting
location: Issawiya, Mount Scopus, Jerusalem
actor_as_reported: Israeli police
event_categories: access restriction; road closure; civilian shooting; killing
affected_people_or_estimate: One Arab villager killed on 2 June; identity and age not stated; no displacement count
evidence_summary: UNTSO's Chief of Staff reported that Israel closed the only reasonable road used by Issawiya villagers on 1 June. On 2 June, an UN observer saw Israeli police fire during a confrontation after villagers were prevented from using the road; one villager fell and died. The observer reported no firearms were produced during the scuffle. The report separately records unresolved claims about the earlier 26 May firefight.
evidence_status: Contemporaneous UN observer report; direct observation of 2 June shooting and reported road closure; initial 26 May firing attribution disputed
legal_status: Potential unlawful use of force and restrictions on civilian movement warrant legal review; UNTSO findings are not a criminal judgment
scope_decision: Include Israeli police actions directly observed/reported; exclude other-party fire and do not attribute the 26 May exchange's initiation to Israel
limitations: UNTSO report does not identify the villager or establish annual displacement. Main 26 May incident was a mixed firing exchange with initial fire attribution unresolved; this row does not count it as an Israeli attack.

event_name: Israeli police firing at Issawiya roadblock
location: Road between Issawiya and Mount Scopus, Jerusalem
actor_as_reported: Israeli police (according to Israeli spokesman reported by JTA)
event_categories: roadblock; police firing; reported injury
affected_people_or_estimate: One person described as an Arab/Jordanian was reported wounded; civilian status and identity not established
evidence_summary: JTA reported the Israeli spokesman's account that police fired after a group continued toward a roadblock on the road used by Issawiya villagers; one person was reported wounded. The same report attributes claims of armed marchers and Jordanian direction to Israeli officials; these claims are not independently verified there.
evidence_status: Contemporary foreign press report relaying Israeli official claims; separate from the UN-observed fatal shooting on 2 June
legal_status: Alleged use of force; available report alone does not establish whether force was lawful or identify the wounded person
scope_decision: Include as a clearly attributed Israeli police firing report; do not treat the official account as independently established fact
limitations: JTA report is Israeli-source framing and does not independently verify the alleged weapons, command, identity, civilian status or injury details.

event_name: Israeli government confiscation of Tamra plots for IDP resettlement
location: Tamra, Galilee, Israel
actor_as_reported: Israeli government
event_categories: land confiscation; state resettlement policy; internal displacement context
affected_people_or_estimate: About 56 plots reportedly confiscated; no affected household/person count given
evidence_summary: Palestinian researcher Nihad Boqa’i reports that the government confiscated about 56 plots from Tamra in October 1958 to resettle internally displaced Palestinians, citing Hillel Cohen (2001). The article says nearby Judaida and al-Jish land was also taken months later, but those actions are not dated precisely enough to include in this 1958 row.
evidence_status: Secondary Palestinian scholarship citing Cohen and Israeli State Archives Housing Ministry file 4410/61621
legal_status: Land/property and resettlement practices warrant further legal and archival review; source does not establish displacement of Tamra residents or a criminal finding
scope_decision: Include as state land-policy evidence; do not count 56 plots as displaced people or claim Tamra residents were removed
limitations: Underlying Cohen study and archive file not yet reviewed; no individual plots, owners, compensation or resettled families identified; no annual displacement total.

event_name: Israeli jet incursion and air combat over UAR territory
location: Sinai/UAR airspace, south of the Israel-Egypt frontier; outside Palestine proper
actor_as_reported: Israeli jet fighters
event_categories: military airspace violation; air combat
affected_people_or_estimate: No casualties reported in reviewed record
evidence_summary: The Egyptian-Israel Mixed Armistice Commission found Israeli jets crossed the international frontier and engaged in air combat over UAR territory. Its decision was quoted in the Security Council record and condemned Israel as a serious violation.
evidence_status: Commission finding; no criminal adjudication
legal_status: Mixed Armistice Commission found a serious violation of the armistice; no individual criminal finding
scope_decision: Include as Israeli state military action in the broader regional file; mark event outside Palestine proper
limitations: No casualty count identified; Commission record was reached in Israel's absence.

event_name: Israeli patrol attack on Bedouin family at Karm Abu Shaluf
location: South of Rafah, across frontier in UAR/Egyptian territory; outside Palestine proper
actor_as_reported: Four-man armed Israeli patrol
event_categories: cross-border armed attack; killing; civilian harm
affected_people_or_estimate: Two killed: Fatima Mohammed, 25, and four-year-old Silmi Ide; one woman wounded
evidence_summary: The Commission found an armed Israeli patrol crossed the international frontier and attacked a Bedouin family. Its investigation cited tracks, blood, bodies and Hebrew-marked ammunition and condemned Israel.
evidence_status: Commission investigation and finding
legal_status: Commission found serious armistice violation and condemned Israel; no criminal trial
scope_decision: Include as Israeli state action in regional dataset; explicitly outside Palestine proper
limitations: Decision made in Israel's absence after its 1956 boycott; not a criminal judgment.

event_name: Israeli armed-group ambush in UAR territory
location: Wadi Sirami, Sinai/UAR territory, about 3 km across international frontier; outside Palestine proper
actor_as_reported: Trained Israeli armed group
event_categories: cross-border armed attack; ambush; killing; injury
affected_people_or_estimate: Two of four UAR subjects killed; one wounded
evidence_summary: The Commission found a trained Israeli group crossed about 3 km into UAR territory and ambushed four UAR subjects with small-arms fire. It found a serious violation and condemned Israel.
evidence_status: Commission finding
legal_status: Commission found serious armistice violation; no criminal adjudication
scope_decision: Include as Israeli state military action in regional file; outside Palestine proper
limitations: Commission decision in Israel's absence; evidence mentions two auxiliary policemen among dead, but identity relation to casualty count unclear; do not double-count.

event_name: Reported border-patrol clash near Egyptian frontier
location: Near Egyptian border in southern Israel; exact location unspecified
actor_as_reported: Israeli Army patrol, as reported by an Israeli army spokesman to JTA
event_categories: reported shooting; killing; capture; injury
affected_people_or_estimate: Israeli spokesman reported two Egyptians killed and three wounded and captured
evidence_summary: JTA reported the Israeli army spokesman's account that a patrol spotted five alleged infiltrators and exchanged fire after they were challenged. No Israeli patrol casualties were reported.
evidence_status: Single contemporary foreign press report relaying a party's claim
legal_status: No independent investigation or legal finding located
scope_decision: Retain as provisional Israeli-action lead with actor's claims clearly attributed; distinguish from established facts
limitations: All event details and casualty count come from Israeli army spokesman; no independent corroboration located.

event_name: Expulsion and violent displacement of Azazme Bedouin
location: From Israeli-controlled Negev across international frontier into UAR/Sinai
actor_as_reported: Israeli troops
event_categories: forced displacement; killing; burning of tents; property deprivation; border shooting
affected_people_or_estimate: About 350 Azazme Bedouin expelled (Commission estimate); deaths reported but not fully enumerated; one person separately found killed by Israeli fire on UAR territory
evidence_summary: The Commission found Israeli troops expelled about 350 Azazme Bedouin, killed some, burned tents and deprived them of property, compelling flight. It separately found one Bedouin killed by Israeli fire across the border. It described treatment as harsh and cruel and condemned Israel.
evidence_status: International Commission finding; contemporary foreign press reports related lethal patrol action; Israel response recorded separately
legal_status: Commission found violations of Security Council and armistice provisions; no criminal adjudication
scope_decision: Include as Israeli state action and primary displacement record; about 350 is the Commission estimate, not a complete annual total
limitations: Israel disputed Commission process and account; source says 'some' killed without a total; JTA's three deaths may overlap and are not added. Israeli officer killing and Israel's counter-account are context.

event_name: Israeli fighters intercept UAR commercial airliner over Gulf of Aqaba
location: Gulf of Aqaba; outside Palestine proper
actor_as_reported: Four Israeli fighter aircraft, as found by Commission
event_categories: military aircraft interception; alleged firing; attempted forced landing
affected_people_or_estimate: No injuries reported; airliner continued to Cairo
evidence_summary: JTA reported Commission strongly blamed Israel for an attack by four Israeli fighters and said the planes fired in an attempt to force a UAR airliner to land in Israel. The plane continued to Cairo; Israel denied that its aircraft fired.
evidence_status: Contemporary foreign press report of Commission finding and Israeli denial
legal_status: Commission called it a flagrant breach of the armistice and demanded no repetition; no criminal adjudication
scope_decision: Include as Israeli state military action in wider regional file; outside Palestine proper
limitations: Commission decision itself not separately retrieved in this pass; JTA is the available account; no casualties reported.

event_name: Reported expulsion of more than 100 Azazme Bedouin into Jordan
location: Negev to Jordan; exact date/location unspecified
actor_as_reported: Israeli authorities, as alleged by Bedouin and reported by JTA
event_categories: alleged forced displacement; border expulsion
affected_people_or_estimate: More than 100 claimed in contemporary report
evidence_summary: JTA reported a Jordanian complaint alleging more than 100 Bedouin expelled from the Negev into Jordan. A follow-up reported Israel offered screening for possible readmission subject to proof of residence/citizenship.
evidence_status: Contemporary foreign press report of complaint and state response
legal_status: No independent or Commission finding located in this initial review
scope_decision: Include as provisional expulsion allegation; separate from September expulsions into UAR and do not sum
limitations: Whether this group overlaps September Operation Hagar expulsions remains unresolved; identities/timing not established; not a verified total.

event_name: Israeli jet incursion and air combat over Sinai
location: UAR airspace over Sinai, beyond international frontier; outside Palestine proper
actor_as_reported: At least four Israeli jet aircraft
event_categories: military airspace violation; air combat
affected_people_or_estimate: No casualties reported in reviewed Commission decision
evidence_summary: The Commission found at least four Israeli jets crossed the frontier deep into UAR airspace and engaged in air combat after interception; it condemned Israel and demanded the conduct cease.
evidence_status: International Commission finding
legal_status: Commission found serious armistice violation; no criminal adjudication
scope_decision: Include as Israeli state military action in regional file; outside Palestine proper
limitations: Decision adopted in Israel's absence; no casualties reported.

event_name: Negev Bedouin military administration and settlement-law planning
location: Negev, Israel
actor_as_reported: Israeli government and appointed committees
event_categories: military administration; land policy; settlement planning; proposed relocation
affected_people_or_estimate: No displaced-person count; reviewed source describes policy proposals, not completed removal
evidence_summary: Historical scholarship describes August 1959 decision to continue military administration and draft settlement law, with December committee support for land registration in southern Negev and legislation concerning settlement in the east. Implementation and completed relocation are not established.
evidence_status: Peer-reviewed historical scholarship; policy planning rather than event-level finding
legal_status: No legal adjudication or proven land seizure in reviewed evidence
scope_decision: Include as expansionist/state-policy context only; not a completed displacement or settlement event
limitations: Based on secondary scholarship; underlying committee records not reviewed; no affected household count.

event_name: Israeli military attack and near-total destruction of Khirbat at Tawafiq
location: Khirbat at Tawafiq, southern Israel-Syria demilitarized zone
actor_as_reported: Regular Israeli armed forces
event_categories: military attack; artillery and mortar fire; village destruction; killing; injury
affected_people_or_estimate: UNTSO/MAC record: two Arab deaths and two wounded; JTA reported about 50 houses leveled
evidence_summary: UNTSO Chief of Staff submitted a report following observer investigation. The Israel-Syrian Mixed Armistice Commission said the regular Israeli army attacked the village overnight, which it said had only a protective trench and barbed wire, causing near-total destruction, two killed and two wounded. It condemned Israel and found an armistice violation. JTA contemporaneously reported that approximately 50 houses were leveled. Israel said it acted to dislodge an illegal Syrian military post; preserve that claim as Israel's account.
evidence_status: UN observer investigation; Mixed Armistice Commission finding; contemporary foreign reporting; Israeli party response
legal_status: Commission condemned attack and found flagrant violation of Article V, paras 5(a)-(b) of General Armistice Agreement; no criminal adjudication
scope_decision: Include as Israeli state military action against a village; preserve Israeli claim and Commission/observer findings separately
limitations: Commission meeting proceeded without Israeli delegation; count and destruction description derive from UN record, while JTA reports 50 houses; neither source provides a full household displacement count.

event_name: Israeli Air Force overflight of Qunaytirah
location: Qunaytirah area, Syrian territory
actor_as_reported: Four Mystère jet planes identified by UN observer as aircraft used by the Israeli Air Force
event_categories: military airspace violation; hostile act
affected_people_or_estimate: No casualties reported
evidence_summary: A UN military observer identified four Mystère jets, a type used by the Israeli Air Force, flying over Qunaytirah in Syrian territory for about half an hour. The Israel-Syrian Mixed Armistice Commission condemned the hostile act and found violations of the armistice.
evidence_status: UN observer finding adopted by Mixed Armistice Commission
legal_status: Commission found violations of Articles III(2) and IV(2) of the General Armistice Agreement; no criminal adjudication
scope_decision: Include as Israeli state military action in the regional record; location is Syrian territory, not Palestine proper
limitations: No injury or damage reported in the reviewed finding; resolution adopted without Israeli participation.

event_name: Proposed relocation of Bedouin households from Negev to central mixed cities
location: Negev to Ramle/Lod and Jaffa; proposed destinations
actor_as_reported: Israeli Minister of Agriculture Moshe Dayan and government committee
event_categories: state relocation planning; proposed urbanization; land and population policy
affected_people_or_estimate: Proposal to relocate 500 Bedouin families; implementation and actual number moved not established by reviewed evidence
evidence_summary: Historical scholarship based on archival documents reports that Dayan submitted a July proposal, with IDF and Labor Ministry approval, to relocate 500 Bedouin families to Ramle and Jaffa. The source also records individual requests and administrative planning, but this review does not establish that the 500-family proposal was implemented.
evidence_status: Peer-reviewed historical scholarship based on archival sources; proposed plan, not completed displacement
legal_status: No legal finding or proof of forced implementation in reviewed record
scope_decision: Include as expansionist/state population policy planning; do not count 500 families as displaced persons
limitations: Proposal number describes intended relocation, not completed movement; no verified annual displaced-person count; underlying archival files not independently reviewed here.

event_name: Israeli aircraft machine-gun Bedouin grazing livestock
location: UAR territory beyond the Israel-Egypt frontier; exact grazing location not specified
actor_as_reported: Two Israeli aircraft
event_categories: cross-border air incursion; machine-gun attack; animal killing and injury
affected_people_or_estimate: A few camels and donkeys killed or wounded; no human casualties reported
evidence_summary: The Egyptian-Israel Mixed Armistice Commission found that two Israeli aircraft crossed the international frontier into UAR airspace, spotted a flock of livestock, flew at very low altitude and machine-gunned the animals, killing and wounding a few camels and donkeys.
