The Commission condemned Israel for a hostile and inhuman act.
evidence_status: Contemporaneous Mixed Armistice Commission finding; text transmitted to the Security Council
legal_status: Commission condemnation and armistice finding; no criminal adjudication; no human injuries reported
scope_decision: Include as documented Israeli military action in the regional file; explicitly outside Palestine proper
limitations: The Commission did not enumerate the animals; decision was based on complaint and investigative record, not a criminal trial.

event_name: Israeli parade rehearsal deploys prohibited heavy weapons in Jerusalem
location: Israeli-controlled sector of Jerusalem along the Jordan-Israel Armistice Demarcation Line
actor_as_reported: Israeli authorities and military
event_categories: military deployment; heavy weapons; armistice violation; political assertion of control
affected_people_or_estimate: No casualties or displacement reported
evidence_summary: After UN military observers investigated Jordan's complaint, the Jordan-Israel Mixed Armistice Commission found heavy weapons in excess of the armistice limits on Israel's side of the line during the parade rehearsal, including a Centurion tank, Sherman tanks and 105mm/155mm artillery. It found a breach, condemned Israel and called for measures to prevent recurrence. Israel defended the event as a peaceful ceremony and cited prior Jordanian parades.
evidence_status: UN military observer investigation; Mixed Armistice Commission finding; Israeli response preserved in Security Council debate
legal_status: Commission found a breach of the General Armistice Agreement; Security Council Resolution 162 endorsed its decision and called on Israel to comply; no criminal adjudication
scope_decision: Include as Israeli state military action and documented armistice breach in Jerusalem; the finding is specifically about the rehearsal
limitations: Commission decision addressed the 17 March rehearsal and weapons present that morning; does not establish civilian harm or an additional casualty count.

event_name: Israeli military parade proceeds in Jerusalem after Commission condemnation
location: Israeli-controlled sector of Jerusalem
actor_as_reported: Israeli government and armed forces
event_categories: military parade; display of heavy weapons; continuation after UN condemnation
affected_people_or_estimate: No casualties or displacement reported in reviewed report
evidence_summary: JTA reported that Israel held its Independence Day military parade in Jerusalem on 20 April, after the Commission condemned the 17 March rehearsal and the Security Council urged compliance. The report describes tanks and artillery, including U.S.-made 106mm recoilless guns mounted on jeeps. Israel maintained that the parade was ceremonial; the Commission's specific breach finding concerned the March rehearsal, and this register does not treat that finding as a separate adjudication of the April parade.
evidence_status: Contemporary foreign press report read alongside UN Commission/Security Council action and Israel's stated position
legal_status: Security Council Resolution 162 endorsed the Commission decision regarding the March breach; reviewed record does not establish a separate Commission ruling on the 20 April parade
scope_decision: Include as consequential Israeli military display in occupied/divided Jerusalem; distinguish the confirmed March ruling from the April event report
limitations: JTA says 300,000 attended and reports equipment displayed; it does not establish weapon ammunition status or a new legal finding regarding parade day.

event_name: Israeli retaliatory raid on Syrian positions and villages near Lake Tiberias
location: Nuquieb, Squofie, Fiq, El-Douga and nearby Syrian positions, east of Lake Tiberias; Israel-Syria demilitarized-zone area
actor_as_reported: Israeli regular armed forces, including ground troops, artillery, armoured boats and air force
event_categories: cross-border/DMZ military raid; mortar and artillery fire; air attack; destruction of positions; temporary civilian flight
affected_people_or_estimate: UNTSO report gives no verified casualty total; it records villagers fleeing from Nuquieb to El-Koursi; number displaced unknown
evidence_summary: The UNTSO Chief of Staff's report describes the preceding clashes, the Israeli military action overnight on 16–17 March and an incomplete UN observer investigation. The Israeli Defence Forces said they destroyed Syrian positions after attacks on boats and fishermen. Syrian complaints described Israeli fire against villages and military posts; UN observers documented craters, bullet/projectile evidence and the departure of villagers from Nuquieb. On 9 April, the Security Council determined that Israel's attack constituted a flagrant violation of Resolution 111 (1956). U.S. State Department records called it a retaliatory raid and said Washington opposed the use of such raids.
evidence_status: UNTSO investigation with limits; Security Council determination; contemporary U.S. diplomatic record; JTA reporting of the Israeli action and competing claims
legal_status: Security Council Resolution 171 determined a flagrant violation of prior resolution 111 and called on Israel to refrain; not a criminal judgment. UNTSO said observers could not closely follow the night operation and described its investigation as incomplete.
scope_decision: Include as Israeli state military action; preserve Syrian and Israeli accounts; count no casualties or displaced persons beyond what UNTSO directly reports
limitations: UNTSO records preceding Syrian fire as well as Israeli fire and says it could not establish all firing origins; no verified casualty count for Syrians or number of displaced villagers in the reviewed report.

event_name: Israeli aircraft implicated in aerial battle over Qunaytirah; child slightly injured by falling fuel tank
location: Qunaytirah, Syrian territory
actor_as_reported: Israeli Mystère jets, alleged in Syrian complaint and identified as aircraft type used by Israel
event_categories: airspace violation; aerial combat; falling aircraft fuel tanks; child injury
affected_people_or_estimate: One child slightly wounded; no death reported
evidence_summary: UNTSO observers clearly saw an aerial dogfight of six aircraft in Syrian airspace. Syria complained that four Israeli Mystère jets had earlier violated Syrian airspace and engaged Syrian aircraft; its complaint said four fuel tanks fell on Syrian territory and a child was hit. The UN observer was shown four tanks, one bearing a French inscription, and saw the boy in hospital with slight injury. The report does not conclusively establish which aircraft dropped the tanks or the full sequence.
evidence_status: UN observer observation plus Syrian complaint and physical evidence; attribution remains provisional
legal_status: No separate Security Council or criminal finding on this specific 20 March event identified in this pass
scope_decision: Include as a provisional Israeli-attribution incident with the disputed attribution visible
limitations: The observer could not identify aircraft during the dogfight; the account that Israeli aircraft dropped the tanks comes from Syria's complaint, while the tanks and child's injury were observed.

event_name: Police arrests during opposition to Beit Netofa water-pipeline excavation
location: Beit Netofa area, Lower Galilee, Israel
actor_as_reported: Israeli police
event_categories: arrest; public-order response; state water infrastructure project
affected_people_or_estimate: JTA reports an unspecified number of Arab residents arrested; no charges, detention duration or household displacement count given
evidence_summary: JTA reported that excavation for a water pipeline resumed under heavy police guard after a series of night arrests of Arabs said to be trying to incite villagers to oppose the work by force. The report does not provide names, exact arrest count, charges or detainee outcomes.
evidence_status: Contemporary foreign press report; official framing of alleged incitement not independently verified
legal_status: No judicial or human-rights finding located; do not infer unlawful detention or abuse from the report alone
scope_decision: Include as a provisional arrest and development-policy record; keep the official characterization attributed and count unspecified
limitations: Single short press report; no independent investigation, court records, named detainees or displacement evidence located in this pass.

event_name: Two 17-year-old Palestinian Arab citizens sentenced to prison on espionage convictions
location: Beersheba District Court, Israel
actor_as_reported: Israeli District Court and prison authorities
event_categories: criminal prosecution; imprisonment of minors
affected_people_or_estimate: Two teenagers, each sentenced to six years; JTA does not name them
evidence_summary: JTA reported that two 17-year-old Israeli Arabs were sentenced to six years each for espionage. The dispatch says they told the court they had been detained by Egyptian intelligence during a trip to Gaza, questioned about Israeli projects and military sites, and recruited before returning to Israel. This row records Israeli prosecution and imprisonment as a detention event; it does not allege abuse or adjudicate the truth of the espionage case.
evidence_status: Contemporary foreign press report of a court sentence and defendants' statements
legal_status: Court convictions reported; no appeal, underlying judgment or later outcome reviewed
scope_decision: Include as a detention/capture record requested by the project; do not present the imprisonment as a war crime or imply mistreatment without evidence
limitations: No names, trial transcript, counsel details, appeal or prison-condition evidence in the JTA dispatch.

event_name: Dardara/Ashmura cultivation dispute and firing
location: Central Israel-Syria demilitarized zone near Dardara and Houle Lake
actor_as_reported: Israeli soldiers and armed guard; Israeli bulldozer; kibbutz Dardara
event_categories: armed entry; disputed cultivation/land-use; firing; crop/land damage risk
affected_people_or_estimate: Syrian patrol reported under fire; casualties not established
evidence_summary: UNTSO report S/5401 records Syria's complaint that Israeli soldiers took position and a bulldozer entered disputed parcel, then Israelis opened fire from Dardara and other positions. Two Syrian witnesses described the incident; they supplied fragments of .5-inch heavy-machine-gun projectiles. The Mixed Armistice Commission chairman noted the land was mapped as Jewish-owned but had not recently been cultivated, and said legality was difficult to determine; Syrians invoked a status quo agreement.
evidence_status: UN investigation of Syrian complaint with witness statements and physical evidence; party complaint; legal status of cultivation unresolved
legal_status: No adjudication of attack legality or land title; the UN report documents an exchange and disputed land use, not an established war crime
scope_decision: Include Israeli military/armed-guard activity and expansion/land-use context; retain Syrian allegations as allegations and the chairman's uncertainty
limitations: No established casualty count; boundaries/status quo and legality of cultivation unresolved; does not establish displacement.

event_name: Israeli firing in central demilitarized zone; damage near El Sayyadi
location: Central Israel-Syria demilitarized zone, including El Sayyadi village, Darbashiya, Wadi El Fazir and Dardara
actor_as_reported: Israeli armored vehicles and military personnel; Syrian forces also exchanged fire
event_categories: military firing; damage to civilian home and crops; armistice violation
affected_people_or_estimate: No verified human casualty count; one house damaged, crops burnt in several areas
evidence_summary: UNTSO report S/5401 records witness statements that Israeli fire began toward El Sayyadi around 1310, damaged a house and burned crops; UN observers themselves saw burnt fields at several named locations and small-arms damage at El Sayyadi. The report also records an Israeli armored personnel carrier in a defensive area in violation of the General Armistice Agreement, and observed Israeli fire at 1054 in a separate exchange. Other exchanges were initiated by Syrian fire or had unknown initiator; the full day was contested.
evidence_status: International observer report with on-site damage observations, witness accounts, party complaints, and radio logs
legal_status: UNTSO identified an armistice violation by an Israeli APC; it did not determine that every Israeli use of fire was unlawful or assign a casualty total
scope_decision: Include documented Israeli fire and physical damage while distinguishing disputed sequence and reciprocal exchanges; do not classify the entire battle as a proven war crime
limitations: The report's chronology contains differing local/GMT time references; no casualty or displacement total; air engagement aircraft nationality not identified.

event_name: ‘Ali Mohamad Mar’i Hammad detained after travel without military permit
location: From Kafr Danon to Zichron Ya’akov; police station location not specified
actor_as_reported: Israeli Military Government permit office and police
event_categories: movement restriction; detention; military administration
affected_people_or_estimate: One Palestinian citizen, held about 1.5 days; later reported fine of two Israeli pounds
evidence_summary: Akevot's archival article summarizes a Hebrew intelligence/administrative digest of Arabic-language press: the Military Government office denied Hammad a travel permit despite a workers' council holiday approval; he traveled and was detained by police at the facility for a day and a half. Hammad later said he was tried by a Nazareth military court and fined two Israeli pounds.
evidence_status: Later archival summary of 29 November 1963 Arabic press plus later testimony
legal_status: Detention and movement restriction documented in archival summary; no finding of illegality or abuse; no torture allegation
scope_decision: Include as a Palestinian citizen detention and movement-control record; do not label war crime without further legal evidence
limitations: Original Arabic news item and military-court record not reviewed; exact arrest and hearing dates, legal basis, and later outcome unverified.

event_name: Reported Israeli firing at Arab farmers and Syrian posts
location: Israel-Syria Armistice Demarcation Line, including Dardara sector
actor_as_reported: Israeli Armed Forces (as alleged in Syrian government letter)
event_categories: small-arms fire; interference with cultivation; armistice-line incident
affected_people_or_estimate: Arab farmers; no casualty count stated
evidence_summary: Syria's 8 July letter to the Security Council alleged Israeli forces fired automatic weapons at Arab farmers to harass them and prevent ploughing on 2 July, then fired intermittently at Syrian posts through 6 July. The letter said Israeli armored cars fired on a Syrian post on 6 July and Syria filed an urgent complaint.
evidence_status: Contemporaneous Security Council document reproducing Syrian government's complaint; no independent investigation located for this record
legal_status: Allegations not independently verified in the reviewed sources; no war-crime or legal determination
scope_decision: Include as a clearly attributed allegation of Israeli fire and interference with cultivation; do not present the account as an independently verified finding
limitations: No names, injuries, damage or displacement counts; Israel's response and UN observer findings not located in this scan.

event_name: Interministerial planning for Negev Bedouin building sites and relocation policy
location: Negev, Israel
actor_as_reported: Israeli government interministerial committee and Israel Land Administration
event_categories: state planning; Bedouin settlement/relocation policy; land administration
affected_people_or_estimate: No completed moves or affected-person count established for 1964
evidence_summary: Historical research citing archival committee records says an interministerial directors-general committee was established on 19 April 1964 to prepare a proposal regarding building sites for Negev Bedouin. This is evidence of state planning, not evidence that relocation was carried out that year.
evidence_status: Later academic historical study citing archival records
legal_status: No contemporaneous displacement count or finding of coercion for this 1964 committee action
scope_decision: Include as expansion/relocation-policy context, explicitly separated from completed displacement
limitations: Underlying committee file not reviewed directly here; no number of people moved or forced out established.

event_name: Tel El-Qadi/Nukheila fighting and Israeli air and tank attacks
location: Northern Israel-Syria armistice line; Tel El-Qadi, Nukheila, Tel Azaziat, Banias, Abbasieh and nearby Syrian positions
actor_as_reported: Israeli military patrols, tanks and Israeli Air Force; Syrian forces also engaged
event_categories: armored incursion allegation; exchange of fire; air and tank attacks; village damage; civilian casualties
affected_people_or_estimate: Syrian liaison reported 7 killed and 26 injured, most civilians; Israeli report recorded 3 soldiers killed, 9 wounded and 2 kibbutz members injured
evidence_summary: UNTSO observers logged the stages of the clash. The report says the initial Syrian fire was directed at an Israeli patrol after an Israeli armored personnel carrier reportedly entered about 50 metres into Syrian territory; the boundary and road alignment were disputed. Israeli aircraft then bombed and strafed Syrian positions, and Israeli tanks shelled Tel Azaziat. Observers recorded damage at Nukheila and Abbasieh and bomb evidence near Massada; they could not inspect every claimed site, and the Syrian casualty figures came from the Syrian liaison officer. The incident followed Israeli reconstruction of a boundary track and drainage ditch in the disputed Tel El-Qadi area.
evidence_status: Contemporaneous UNTSO observer report with observation-post logs, field inspection and party complaints
legal_status: No final legal judgment on the entire battle in the report; UNTSO documents the initial Syrian fire after reported Israeli APC entry and separately logs Israeli attacks and observed damage; Security Council draft resolution deplored renewed military action and regretted deaths on both sides but was not adopted
scope_decision: Include Israeli attacks and territorial/boundary context; distinguish the reported Israeli incursion, Syrian opening fire, Israeli air/tank strikes, civilian impacts, and limits on site inspection
limitations: Seven Syrian deaths and 26 injuries reported by Syrian liaison; most described as civilians, not all identities independently verified; some strike sites inaccessible; no displacement count.

event_name: Israeli fire at Syrian cultivators and agricultural equipment
location: Israel-Syria demilitarized zone and Syrian territory near the armistice line
actor_as_reported: Israeli armed forces
event_categories: firing on civilians/cultivators; crop and livestock damage; armistice violation
affected_people_or_estimate: Syrian civilians working land; no human casualty count reported; three oxen killed and one cow wounded according to Syria's complaint
evidence_summary: Syria's complaint reported repeated Israeli fire from 13–18 May at Syrian civilians and cultivators, burning or damaging tractors and crops and killing/wounding livestock. For 13 May, ISMAC's chairman reported after investigation that there was no evidence of Syrian fire, and that Israeli fire targeted equipment and civilians working well inside Syrian territory. He stated that firing from within the demilitarized zone was a serious breach and prohibited weapons in the Israeli sector a flagrant violation of the Armistice Agreement. The later May 15–18 claims are recorded as Syrian allegations, not as individually verified findings.
evidence_status: ISMAC chair's quoted investigation conclusion for 13 May; contemporaneous Syrian government complaint for the wider 13–18 May sequence
legal_status: ISMAC finding establishes no Syrian fire and civilians/equipment as target on 13 May; no human casualties reported; later incidents not independently verified here; no war-crime adjudication
scope_decision: Include documented Israeli fire and civilian/agricultural harm; clearly separate Commission findings for 13 May from Syria's allegations about later dates
limitations: No casualty count for people; subsequent dates 15–18 May rely on Syrian complaint; land status described differently by parties.

event_name: Syrian complaint of Israeli launch firing near El Kursi
location: Lake Tiberias / eastern shore facing El Kursi, Syrian territory
actor_as_reported: Israeli armed launch (as alleged by Syrian government)
event_categories: naval/shore firing; armistice-line incident
affected_people_or_estimate: No casualties reported in the letter
evidence_summary: Syria's 28 May Security Council letter alleged that an Israeli armed launch approached the eastern shore of Lake Tiberias facing El Kursi and fired heavy automatic weapons and mortars across the Armistice Demarcation Line toward Syrian positions for about 15 minutes; it said fire was returned. No separate UNTSO investigation of this specific allegation was located in the current scan.
evidence_status: Contemporaneous diplomatic complaint by Syria
legal_status: Allegation; independent investigation or legal determination not located
scope_decision: Include as an attributed Israeli-action allegation only; exclude the Syrian return fire from this Israel-only dataset
limitations: No casualties or damage count; the account is party-submitted and not independently verified in sources reviewed.

event_name: Israeli raid and demolition of inhabited home in Jordan
location: Jordanian territory across the Armistice Demarcation Line; settlement/village names not specified in the reviewed Commission summary
actor_as_reported: Israeli armed forces
event_categories: cross-border raid; demolition of civilian homes; killing and wounding civilians; firing on patrol
affected_people_or_estimate: Mixed Armistice Commission reported 5 civilians killed (2 men and 3 children, youngest 4) and 5 civilians wounded (2 adults and 3 children, youngest 2); a Jordanian soldier was also wounded
evidence_summary: The Jordan-Israel Mixed Armistice Commission found that Israeli forces crossed the Armistice Demarcation Line on 27 May, demolished an inhabited home and completely destroyed another house with explosives, damaged a third, and fired on a Jordanian routine patrol. It found two men and three children killed and two adults and three children wounded among Jordanian civilians; separately, the patrol incident wounded a Jordanian soldier. The Commission found no evidence Jordan was involved in sabotage against Ramat-Hahovesh and condemned Israel for a flagrant Armistice Agreement violation.
evidence_status: Mixed Armistice Commission investigation and decision transmitted to the Security Council
legal_status: Commission found a flagrant violation of Article III, paragraph 2, of the General Armistice Agreement; it regretted civilian deaths, injuries and property damage. No criminal war-crimes judgment is recorded.
scope_decision: Include as an Israeli military raid against civilian homes; specify the Commission findings and do not conflate Jordanian troops with civilian victims
limitations: The Security Council letter's summary does not identify the affected households or exact village names; no displacement count beyond destroyed homes.

event_name: Mob attack on Ramleh's Arab quarter
location: Ramleh (Ramla), Israel
actor_as_reported: Crowd of Jewish Israeli youths; Israeli police intervened
event_categories: mob attack; assault on Palestinian/Arab citizens; attempted incursion into Arab quarter
affected_people_or_estimate: JTA reported at least 12 Arab residents injured, including women, children and elderly men; 21 youths arrested
evidence_summary: After a Jewish youth died in a traffic collision involving an Arab taxi driver, hundreds of youths assembled after the funeral and attacked Arab residents in the streets, while a larger crowd attempted to enter Ramleh's Arab quarter. JTA reported police stopped the attempt, arrested 21 youths and that at least 12 Arab residents were injured. A PLO memorandum transmitted by Syria described a mob of more than 500 and alleged intent to destroy the quarter; that characterization is attributed to the memorandum, not treated as independently established intent.
evidence_status: Contemporaneous JTA report; PLO memorandum transmitted as UN document S/6731
legal_status: Mob violence documented by contemporary reporting; no state direction or criminal legal finding established; police intervention and arrests also reported
scope_decision: Include the Israeli civilian mob violence against Arab residents; identify mob perpetrators separately from state actors and record police response
limitations: JTA reports at least 12 injured; PLO account's crowd size and asserted intent are not independently verified; no evidence of displacement.

event_name: Israeli army raid on Houla and Meiss El Jabal
location: Southern Lebanon, Houla and Meiss El Jabal
actor_as_reported: Israeli Army regular forces in uniform
event_categories: cross-border military incursion; demolition; destruction of water source; civilian death
affected_people_or_estimate: Lebanon reported one woman killed, two houses destroyed and neighboring homes damaged; a spring and three reservoirs destroyed; no population displacement count
evidence_summary: Lebanon told the Security Council Israeli regular forces entered Lebanese territory and sabotaged sites at Houla and Meiss El Jabal; it said UN observers investigated on location and photographed evidence. Lebanon reported that a woman was crushed when a neighboring house collapsed and that a spring with three reservoirs was dynamited. Israel's own Security Council letter acknowledged an army 'warning action' after earlier sabotage attacks it attributed to armed groups crossing from Lebanon, and said its unit blew up an empty house and water installation. A U.S. State Department record shows the U.S. Assistant Secretary reminded Israel's foreign minister of Washington's opposition to unilateral cross-border action.
evidence_status: Lebanese Security Council complaint reporting UNTSO on-site verification; Israeli government acknowledgment and stated reprisal rationale; contemporaneous U.S. diplomatic record
legal_status: No independent legal adjudication located; Israel acknowledged the action but disputed characterization and described a warning action; civilian death and damage details are from Lebanon's account
scope_decision: Include Israeli action in Lebanon and its civilian/property impacts; preserve Israel's stated rationale and U.S. opposition as context, without implying approval or legality
limitations: No displacement count or full casualty list; Lebanon's impact details and Israel's justification are party accounts, though UN observers reportedly verified physical damage.

event_name: State demolition program targeting abandoned Palestinian villages
location: Inside Israel; villages depopulated in 1948
actor_as_reported: Israel Land Administration and state demolition contractors
event_categories: destruction of Palestinian village fabric; property destruction; post-displacement erasure/landscape transformation
affected_people_or_estimate: Multiple abandoned villages; exact 1965 count and number of structures not established here; residents had been displaced before this period
evidence_summary: Historian Aron Shai's peer-reviewed study traces a state program initiated by the Israel Land Administration in spring 1965 to demolish houses in Palestinian Arab villages abandoned during the 1948 war; the program continued through 1969. The record treats this as destruction of villages after their inhabitants had already been displaced, not as new 1965 displacement or an annualized count.
evidence_status: Peer-reviewed historical research drawing on Israeli state archives
legal_status: No legal judgment on the demolition program in the cited study; the affected villages were already abandoned following 1948 displacement
scope_decision: Include as multi-year state land/settlement and erasure context; do not count it as 1965 displacement or attribute the whole 1965–1969 program to 1965 alone
limitations: This is a multi-year record; no 1965-specific village or structure total is asserted, and no new displaced-person count is established.

event_name: Israeli raid and house demolitions at Rafat
location: Rafat, Hebron district, Jordan-administered West Bank
actor_as_reported: Israeli regular armed forces
event_categories: cross-border military raid; destruction of civilian homes; damage to police post; injury to soldiers; temporary civilian flight
affected_people_or_estimate: Commission found 18 civilian houses completely demolished and three slightly damaged; village residents escaped; two Jordanian soldiers wounded; four horses killed; no civilian casualties found
evidence_summary: The Jordan-Israel Mixed Armistice Commission, based on UN military-observer investigation, found Israeli regular forces crossed the Armistice Demarcation Line and attacked Rafat and the Rujm el Madfa'a police post on 29–30 April. It found 18 houses demolished, three damaged, that residents escaped, two soldiers wounded, and four horses killed. The Commission condemned the action as a serious and flagrant General Armistice Agreement violation. Jordan’s initial Security Council complaint alleged 19 houses destroyed and additional civilian deaths in a separate operation farther east; those claims are kept separate.
evidence_status: UN military-observer investigation and Mixed Armistice Commission decision transmitted in Security Council document S/7333
legal_status: Commission found a flagrant armistice violation and condemned the attack; it found no civilian casualties at Rafat. No criminal war-crimes judgment; no count of people temporarily displaced.
scope_decision: Include the verified Israeli military demolition and escape of residents; do not attribute the separate Sheikh Hussein/Tel el Arba'in casualty list to Rafat or count house destruction as a displacement total.
limitations: Jordan’s initial complaint and the Commission’s final findings differ slightly in house counts; Commission found no civilian casualties at Rafat. Population and duration of flight not established.

event_name: Israeli raid on Tel el Arba'in and Jisr Sheikh Hussein police post
location: Jordanian territory east of the Jordan River, near Tel el Arba'in and Jisr Sheikh Hussein
actor_as_reported: Israeli regular armed forces
event_categories: cross-border military attack; firing on civilians; civilian deaths and injuries; home destruction; attack on police post
affected_people_or_estimate: Jordan-Israel Mixed Armistice Commission decision listed 11 civilians killed and three wounded; approximately 10 stone houses badly damaged or demolished
evidence_summary: The Commission's adopted decision on Jordanian complaint M-222 found Israeli forces crossed the Armistice Demarcation Line, attacked the civilian village of Tel el Arba'in and bombarded the Jisr Sheikh Hussein police post with 105mm and 106mm recoilless guns and other weapons. It listed 11 civilians killed, three civilians wounded and approximately 10 homes badly damaged or demolished, and stated that there was no evidence the named civilian victims were armed. Jordan's initial 1 May complaint gave a lower provisional toll of at least eight killed and described four houses destroyed; the commission investigation supplies the later named list.
evidence_status: UN military-observer investigation and adopted Mixed Armistice Commission decision, circulated as Security Council document S/7325
legal_status: Commission found the victims had been killed or wounded by fire directed by the attackers and found no proof any was armed; condemned the attack as a flagrant armistice violation. No criminal court finding or annual displacement count.
scope_decision: Include as a distinct Israeli military operation and civilian casualty record; preserve the initial complaint and later commission findings as separate stages of evidence.
limitations: The Commission could not determine the exact number of homes where clustered structures were totally destroyed; no count of residents displaced. Location was then Jordanian territory, not yet under Israeli occupation.

event_name: Israeli army raid on As Samu and surrounding southern Hebron villages
location: As Samu and nearby villages, southern Hebron district, Jordan-administered West Bank
actor_as_reported: Israel Defense Forces / Israeli regular armed forces
event_categories: large-scale cross-border raid; demolition of homes and civilian infrastructure; civilian and military deaths and injuries; capture and detention of Jordanian soldiers; temporary flight
affected_people_or_estimate: Corrected UNTSO casualty total: 3 civilians and 15 Jordanian military personnel killed; 17 civilians and 37 military wounded. UN observers saw 125 houses, clinic, six-classroom school and workshop completely demolished; mosque and 28 houses damaged; 20 army trucks, two jeeps and one civilian bus demolished. As Samu population reported as 5,000; number displaced not established.
evidence_summary: UNTSO one-sided investigation conducted in Jordan after Jordanian complaint reported Israeli armored cars opening fire on a police post, Israeli forces crossing the Armistice Demarcation Line, house demolition, civilian injuries and military engagement. Investigators confirmed destruction and casualty certificates. A Jordanian private said Israeli troops captured, blindfolded and evacuated him, interrogated him about military information, and handed him over two days later; no torture was alleged. A Jordanian major also died in Israeli custody despite medical efforts. Israel said its purpose was to demolish empty houses as a warning after a mine killed three Israeli soldiers; it disputed the UN account's scale and sequence. The report's first-distribution count of 97 civilian wounded was formally corrected to 17.
evidence_status: UNTSO investigation S/7593 and Corr.1; Security Council Resolution 228; U.S. FRUS diplomatic records
legal_status: Security Council Resolution 228 deplored loss of life/property, censured Israel for a large-scale military action violating the UN Charter and General Armistice Agreement, and said military reprisals could not be tolerated. This is a UN political/legal determination, not a criminal court judgment. Israeli casualty and operational claims are preserved as party statements.
scope_decision: Include the Israeli state military action and the UN-confirmed civilian impacts; separate civilian from military totals, report the correction of the 97 figure, and treat detention facts without alleging torture. Keep displacement count unknown.
limitations: UN investigation was one-sided within Jordan and Israeli officers did not participate as witnesses; Israel contested the account. Residents fled before/during the raid, but no measured displacement total is supplied. Israeli mine/retaliation rationale is noted but does not alter the actor scope.

event_name: Latrun no-man's-land cultivation dispute and Israeli military entry
location: Latrun sector no-man's-land on Jordan-Israel armistice line
actor_as_reported: Israeli regular forces and Israeli farmers (as alleged by Jordan); Israel disputed the account

limitations: Detailed tractor incursion source is 1965; the 1966 yearbook summary does not specify new 1966 dates, land area, displacement or independent commission findings.

event_name: Israeli aircraft strafing of UNEF convoy

event_name: Destruction/removal at Imwas, Yalu and Beit Nuba

event_name: Gaza refugee men suspected of PLA membership rounded up/removed

event_name: Maghrabi Quarter demolition and clearance

event_name: Extension of Israeli law and municipal administration in East Jerusalem

event_name: Israeli shelling of al-Karameh camp and Jordan Valley villages

scope_decision: Include as attributed allegation with Jordan's named civilian/refugee breakdown and Israel's counterclaims preserved

event_name: Israeli bombardment of al-Karameh and Jordan Valley communities

scope_decision: Include civilian harm and displacement; preserve separate counts and mark the 84 expulsion figure as Jordan's allegation
limitations: Jordan says the refugee camp had been shelled three times in under five weeks; the listed casualties for 15 February are Jordan-reported and should not be merged with the earlier February attack.

event_name: Alleged expulsion of West Bank residents across the Jordan River

event_name: Israeli military operation at al-Karameh
location: al-Karameh and other locations on Jordan's east bank

scope_decision: Include the UN finding and retain Israel's stated rationale; don't assign an unverified total to Palestinian civilians
limitations: The refugee camp's military/civilian status and disaggregated casualties require additional source work.

event_name: Israeli air and artillery attack around Irbid

scope_decision: Include Israeli attack as a reported event with casualty count attributed to Jordan and Israel's self-defence account shown
limitations: Do not report the 30 killed/60 injured as independently verified or civilian-only totals.

event_name: Israeli air attacks on Jordanian territory near Irbid and Salt

legal_status: Resolution 256 condemned the further Israeli military attacks as flagrant violations of the Charter and Resolution 248, deplored deaths and heavy property damage, and warned against repetition; not a criminal court judgment
scope_decision: Include UN condemnation and Jordan's attributed casualty estimate; preserve Israeli target and self-defence claims
limitations: The resolution does not provide a reconciled death or displacement count.

event_name: Shelling of Hula village

legal_status: No criminal finding identified; assess civilian distinction and alleged reprisal separately

event_name: Cross-border shelling of a Lebanese village

event_name: Israeli shelling allegations against Lebanese border areas

legal_status: No legal finding identified

limitations: Underlying complaint and inquiry summaries should be retrieved; crater observation alone does not establish firing source.

event_name: Attempt by Israeli-backed Jewish settlers to establish residence in Hebron

event_name: Israeli customs and civilian-entry decree for occupied Arab territories

event_name: Israeli settlement establishment in the occupied Jordan Valley

event_name: Ramat Eshkol settlement and expropriation in East Jerusalem

event_name: Israeli air attack on Saudi truck convoy near Al-Hasa

event_name: Israeli bombing and shelling allegation at Kufor Asad

event_name: Israeli helicopter-borne raid and abduction in Lebanon

actor_as_reported: Israeli helicopter-borne force
event_categories: cross-border raid; abduction; injuries; property damage
affected_people_or_estimate: Lebanon reported three civilians abducted and four wounded
evidence_summary: The UN Yearbook reports the Israeli force landed in a Lebanese village and kidnapped three civilians, wounding four. UN observers reportedly confirmed two witnesses to abduction and observed destroyed homes, dead sheep and a grenade with Hebrew markings.
evidence_status: UN annual record summarizes complaints and UNTSO field observations; details and village identification require follow-up
legal_status: No judicial finding identified
scope_decision: Include the Israeli raid and abduction; preserve the distinction between reported abduction and observed damage
limitations: Locate the original UNTSO report and complaint letter to verify village name, exact time, house count and identities.

event_name: Arrests, curfew and reported prison beatings during West Bank protests
location: Nablus, East Jerusalem and Gaza, occupied Palestinian territory
actor_as_reported: Israeli police and occupation authorities
event_categories: arrests; curfew; protest suppression; alleged beatings in detention
affected_people_or_estimate: JTA reported 17 students arrested in East Jerusalem on 11 February; UN witness testimony alleged 25 girls were beaten in Nablus and Jerusalem prisons in March
evidence_summary: Contemporary JTA reports document police sealing Nablus's old quarter and arrests of schoolchildren; UN Special Working Group report records witness allegations of beatings in March.
evidence_status: Arrests and curfew contemporaneously reported; prison abuse allegation attributed to testimony
legal_status: No judicial finding identified; the group report summarizes submitted testimony and responses
scope_decision: Include reported Israeli arrests/curfew and separately attributed torture/abuse allegation; do not merge reported counts or imply independently verified abuse
limitations: Clarify precise dates, detention facilities and independent corroboration; not every protest-related death/injury is attributed to Israeli action.

event_name: Deportation of Nablus teacher Kassem Muhammed Hijjawi
location: Nablus to Jordan
actor_as_reported: Israeli occupation authorities
event_categories: deportation; coercive transfer allegation
affected_people_or_estimate: One named teacher reported deported
evidence_summary: JTA reported the deportation and Israeli authorities' accusation that Hijjawi received Jordanian funds to pay teachers not to cooperate with Israeli authorities.
evidence_status: Contemporary report; deportation and accusation reported by JTA; no order or judicial file reviewed
legal_status: No judicial determination identified
scope_decision: Include as an attributed deportation report pending examination of the official order and legal proceedings
limitations: Review the underlying deportation order and any appeal or later return record.

event_name: French Hill settlement establishment
location: North Jerusalem along Jerusalem-Ramallah road, occupied East Jerusalem
actor_as_reported: Israeli government and settlement authorities
event_categories: settlement; land control; territorial expansion
affected_people_or_estimate: UN inventory lists 2,100 housing units and projected/recorded population 15,000 (inventory's later snapshot, not 1969 count)
evidence_summary: A Security Council commission's later inventory dates French Hill to 1969 and describes the site as Arab land and land from a Catholic convent.
evidence_status: Retrospective UN inventory; no exact 1969 expropriation date or acreage established
legal_status: UN Security Council resolution 465 framework describes settlement policy as lacking legal validity; no individual criminal finding
scope_decision: Include settlement establishment as state territorial policy; clearly date the later inventory figures
limitations: Units and population are inventory snapshot values and must not be presented as 1969 occupancy or displacement numbers.

event_name: Israeli ground and air incursion into southern Lebanon
location: Mount Hermon / southern Lebanon
actor_as_reported: Israeli ground forces, air force and artillery
event_categories: cross-border invasion; air and artillery attacks; civilian property destruction and casualties alleged
affected_people_or_estimate: Lebanon reported loss of life and vast property destruction; no verified total in cited UN annual account
evidence_summary: Lebanon told the Security Council that Israeli ground and air forces and heavy artillery attacked three districts in southern Lebanon. Resolution 279 demanded immediate Israeli withdrawal; the Council later characterized the military attack as premeditated, large-scale and carefully planned in Resolution 280. UN reporting said withdrawal was officially confirmed by Lebanon on 13 May.
evidence_status: Security Council resolution demanded withdrawal; Resolution 280 adopted Council characterization; casualty figures remain unspecified in these records
legal_status: UN Security Council resolutions 279 and 280 address state action; no criminal court finding
scope_decision: Include the Israeli operation and UN Council findings; do not impute casualty totals absent source
limitations: Specific villages, civilian death toll and property damage need original inquiry and press sources; Security Council characterization is not a criminal conviction.

event_name: Artillery shelling of four southeastern Lebanese villages
location: Yaroun, Blida, Aitroun and Bent Jbeil, southeastern Lebanon
actor_as_reported: Israeli artillery
event_categories: artillery shelling; alleged civilian deaths and injuries; destruction of homes
affected_people_or_estimate: Lebanon reported 20 killed, 40 wounded and 150 houses destroyed or damaged
evidence_summary: Lebanon's letter to the Security Council reported massive artillery shelling. Resolution 280 had described the Israeli military attack against Lebanon as premeditated, large-scale and carefully planned.
evidence_status: Casualty and damage totals are preliminary figures in a state complaint
legal_status: Security Council Resolution 280 characterized Israeli military action against Lebanon as premeditated, large-scale and carefully planned; no individual criminal finding
scope_decision: Include with the casualty and damage totals explicitly attributed to Lebanon
limitations: The 20 killed are not independently rostered in sources reviewed; check UNTSO incident inquiry and contemporary foreign press.

event_name: Displacement from southern Lebanon during Israeli military campaign
location: Southern Lebanon to other Lebanese regions
actor_as_reported: Israeli military forces (causal attribution in Lebanon's complaint)
event_categories: displacement; forced refuge
affected_people_or_estimate: Lebanon stated that 50,000 persons had been forced to seek refuge in other Lebanese regions; nationality and individual totals unspecified
evidence_summary: Lebanon's 5 June Security Council letter linked the reported displacement to cumulative Israeli actions beginning 12 May.
evidence_status: Attributed estimate by Lebanon; nationality breakdown and independent count absent
legal_status: No judicial finding on individual displacement cases; record as reported population movement
scope_decision: Include as a lead with no claim that all displaced people were Palestinians
limitations: The figure covers people described as displaced in Lebanon; do not classify all as Palestinian or use it as an annual Palestinian displacement count.

event_name: Israeli ground incursion into Lebanon
location: Lebanese territory, reportedly seven kilometres from the border
actor_as_reported: Israeli armed forces
event_categories: cross-border incursion; bombing of civilian installations alleged; military road construction alleged
affected_people_or_estimate: No casualty or displaced-person count established in the reviewed UN record
evidence_summary: Lebanon reported two Israeli infantry companies under air support penetrated seven kilometres and bombed civilian installations. On 5 September the Council adopted Resolution 285 demanding complete and immediate withdrawal. Lebanese authorities later reported withdrawal at 0700 GMT on 6 September; UNTSO said observers were not present to directly observe the withdrawal.
evidence_status: Lebanese allegation and official UN report; withdrawal confirmation relayed by Lebanon, not directly observed
legal_status: Security Council demanded withdrawal; no individual criminal finding
scope_decision: Include as a reported Israeli incursion with the UN demand and observation limitation
limitations: Original Lebanese letter and any site-level UNTSO inspection should be located for casualty/property detail.

event_name: Israeli attacks on Jordanian civilian centres and livelihoods
location: East Bank of Jordan, across the Jordan River and south of the Dead Sea
actor_as_reported: Israeli armed forces
event_categories: air and artillery attacks; attacks on fields, factories and schools; civilian casualties alleged
affected_people_or_estimate: Jordan reported over 90 Jordanians killed or wounded from January through 10 April, a majority described as civilians
evidence_summary: Jordan's Security Council complaint alleged attacks on civilian centres, farmers, shepherds, workers, children at schools and a funeral procession using fighter-bombers, artillery, rockets and sniping.
evidence_status: Attributed aggregate in a state complaint; no incident-by-incident casualty roster in the cited document
legal_status: No judicial finding identified; each event requires separate reconstruction
scope_decision: Include as a dated period-level record and retain Jordan's attribution of the aggregate
limitations: Do not treat the >90 aggregate as a verified fatality count; it combines killed and wounded across multiple incidents.

event_name: Israeli jet attack on civilian bus in northern Jordan Valley
location: Northern Jordan Valley, Jordan
actor_as_reported: Israeli jet aircraft
event_categories: air attack; strafing; civilian deaths and injuries alleged
affected_people_or_estimate: Jordan reported two killed and 13 wounded
evidence_summary: Jordan's letter to the Security Council alleged Israeli aircraft attacked and strafed a bus carrying civilians on a main road.
evidence_status: Contemporaneous state complaint; casualty figures attributed to Jordan
legal_status: No judicial determination identified
scope_decision: Include as an attributed civilian-transport attack allegation; keep the reported toll distinct
limitations: Search for an independent contemporary press dispatch and victim identities.

event_name: Israeli attacks reported across the Jordan Valley and Irbid district
location: Jordan Valley, Irbid and surrounding villages, Jordan
actor_as_reported: Israeli armed forces
event_categories: shelling; bombing; strafing; infiltration; mining; civilian casualties alleged
affected_people_or_estimate: Jordan reported more than 100 attacks during the period; no consolidated victim total in the cited list
evidence_summary: Jordan's 18 August letter listed more than 100 attacks by shelling, bombing, strafing, infiltration and mining; the Security Council yearbook records Israeli attacks and counterclaims throughout this period.
evidence_status: Party complaint summarizes incidents; event-by-event corroboration incomplete
legal_status: No judicial determination identified
scope_decision: Include as a source-tracking record rather than a single verified incident count
limitations: May overlap with the January-April and June bus rows; treat the >100 as a separate period tally, not an additive count of new incidents.

event_name: Israeli military controls, staff detention/deportation and Gaza shelter demolitions affecting UNRWA operations
location: Gaza Strip and West Bank, occupied Palestinian territory
actor_as_reported: Israeli military authorities
event_categories: curfew; screening; detention; deportation; banishment; shelter demolition; arrest of trainees
affected_people_or_estimate: UNRWA reported two staff banished to Sinai for six months; 14 staff arrested in West Bank and 57 in Gaza during the year ending 30 June 1970; shelter demolitions reported without 1970 annual count
evidence_summary: UNRWA's annual report described curfews, screenings, detention and deportation of staff, two six-month banishments to Sinai, demolition of shelters to widen camp roads, and arrests of trainees inside Agency premises.
evidence_status: UN agency reporting and direct operational record; dates span mid-1969 to mid-1970
legal_status: No individual judicial findings; report records operational consequences and alleged practices
scope_decision: Include as a reporting-period record; do not portray all arrests as arbitrary or attribute a calendar-year total without further breakdown
limitations: The 14/57 arrest counts cover 1 July 1969–30 June 1970. The two banishments were staff cases. Specific shelter/person counts by calendar year need original annex extraction.

event_name: Mevo Horon settlement established
location: Modi'in area, West Bank
actor_as_reported: Israeli government and settlement authorities
event_categories: settlement; territorial expansion; land control
affected_people_or_estimate: UN inventory identifies establishment year 1970; no 1970 resident or displacement count
evidence_summary: A later UN settlement list identifies Mevo Horon as a moshav established in 1970.
evidence_status: Retrospective UN inventory; exact site acquisition and 1970 construction record not reviewed
legal_status: No individual criminal determination; settlement policy addressed in later UN findings
scope_decision: Include establishment as Israeli state/settlement policy; separate establishment year from later resident population
limitations: Confirm exact establishment date, land records and non-Israeli contemporary reporting.
